scenario: 面试题：45 分钟设计 WhatsApp，只保留能撑起消息投递主链路的需求。
scenario_en: You have 45 minutes to design WhatsApp, so you only keep the requirements that drive the message-delivery path.
q: WhatsApp 设计题的核心功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are core functional requirements for the WhatsApp design problem? (select all)
options: 音视频通话
创建最多 100 人的群聊
发送 / 接收消息
离线期间的消息在重新上线后仍能收到（30 天内）
options_en: Audio and video calling
Creating group chats with up to one hundred participants
Sending and receiving messages
Receiving messages sent while offline (within thirty days)
why: 核心功能是群聊（上限 100 人）、收发消息、离线补收（30 天）以及消息里带媒体；音视频通话、商家交互、注册资料管理都明确划到范围之外。
why_en: The core requirements are group chats capped at one hundred people, sending and receiving messages, offline delivery within thirty days, and media, while calling is explicitly out of scope.
optionExplanations: 音视频通话被面试官明确划出范围，不必为它设计媒体流转发组件。
属于核心需求，这个 100 人上限后面还决定建群事务和分区设计。
属于核心需求，Chat Server、WebSocket、Inbox 全部围着它转。
属于核心需求，逼出持久化 Inbox 和 30 天 TTL 清理，不能只做纯实时推送。
optionExplanations_en: Calling is explicitly out of scope here, so no media-relay component is needed.
Core requirement — this 100-person cap later drives the create-chat transaction and partition design.
Core requirement — Chat Server, WebSocket, and Inbox all exist to serve this.
Core requirement — it forces a persistent Inbox with 30-day TTL cleanup, not just live push.

scenario: 群聊功能要求最多支持 100 人同时在一个会话里；这个上限后续会反复出现在建群事务、CDN 收益评估和 Pub/Sub 发布次数的计算中。
scenario_en: Group chat must support up to 100 participants in one conversation at once; that cap keeps resurfacing later in the create-chat transaction, the CDN payoff analysis, and the pub/sub publish-count math.
q: 群上限定为 100 人，这个量级最直接支持下面哪个实现判断？
q_en: With the group cap set at 100 people, which implementation judgment does that number most directly support?
options: 100 人已经足够多，必须像 Kafka 一样为每个群单独建一条消息队列
上限只是产品文案，对存储和路由设计没有实际约束
创建群聊时可以把所有参与者记录放进单个 DynamoDB 事务，只有逼近上限的大群才需要分批写
既然上限是 100，Pub/Sub 就必须一律按 chat 而不是 user 分区
options_en: One hundred is large enough that each group needs its own Kafka topic, like a message queue
The cap is only marketing copy with no real constraint on storage or routing
Creating a chat can fit all participant records into a single DynamoDB transaction; only chats near the cap need batched writes
Because the cap is 100, Pub/Sub channels must always be partitioned by chat instead of by user
why: 群上限 100 人和 DynamoDB 单事务 100 items 的上限贴边，所以建群写入默认能塞进一次事务，只有大群逼近上限时才要分批；这个数字后面还会影响 CDN 收益评估和分区发布次数。
why_en: The hundred-person group cap lines up with DynamoDB's hundred-item transaction limit, so creating a chat normally fits one transaction and only needs batching near the cap.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录某个会话里都有哪些成员的关联表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ChatParticipant is the join table recording which members belong to which chat.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志型消息队列，常用于高吞吐事件流的持久化与顺序消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log-based message queue used for durable, ordered consumption of high-throughput event streams.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布订阅模型：发布者把消息发到主题或频道，订阅者从对应主题接收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is a publish-subscribe model where publishers send to topics or channels and subscribers receive from them.

optionExplanations: 把 100 人这种小规模套用成 Kafka 每群一条队列，元数据开销完全不成比例。
否认约束的存在，但这个数字恰好卡在建群写入能否一次性提交的门槛上。
对：小群成员数落在事务写入上限之内，能一次提交；只有逼近这个门槛的大群才要分批。
Pub/Sub 按 user 还是按 chat 分区取决于 1:1 与群聊流量占比，不是由群人数上限直接决定。
optionExplanations_en: Treating a 100-person group like it needs its own Kafka queue is way too heavy for this scale.
This denies the constraint, but 100 sits right at DynamoDB's 100-item single-transaction limit.
Right: 100 lines up with DynamoDB's 100-item transaction cap, so small groups write in one shot and only near-cap groups batch.
Whether Pub/Sub partitions by user or chat depends on the 1:1-vs-group traffic mix, not the group size cap itself.

scenario: 非功能需求要求「消息在中心服务器保存不超过必要时长」，服务端对离线用户未投递消息的保留期限设为 30 天。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirement says messages should not sit on central servers longer than necessary, and the retention window for undelivered messages to offline users is set at thirty days.
q: 30 天这个留存期限，最直接支持下面哪种实现方式？
q_en: Which implementation does that thirty-day retention window most directly support?
options: 在应用代码里永久保存每条消息，仅在读取时按 30 天过滤展示
30 天只是产品说法，数据库层不需要任何过期机制
把所有消息定期打包转移到冷备份，永不删除
给 Inbox、Message 和附件统一设 TTL，交由存储层自动删除
options_en: Keep every message forever in application code and only filter by 30 days at read time
30 days is just marketing copy; the database layer needs no expiry mechanism at all
Periodically move all messages to cold backup storage and never delete them
Set a TTL on Inbox, Message, and attachment rows and let the storage layer auto-delete them
why: TTL 是零运维成本满足「不超必要时长」的实现方式：到期由存储层自动删除，不需要应用代码扫表过滤或人工归档。
why_en: A thirty-day retention window is best implemented as a TTL on the storage rows so the database expires old data automatically, instead of filtering old rows in application code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储条目设置的存活期限，到期后由存储层自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TTL is an expiration time after which the storage layer automatically deletes the item.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

optionExplanations: 永久存储再靠应用过滤，等于自己重造一遍存储层本该做的过期逻辑，还得一直扫表。
否认约束的存在，但 30 天正是「不超必要时长」这条非功能需求本身。
冷备份是「多留一份」不是「按期删除」，既没有省存储也没满足时限要求。
对：给条目统一设 TTL，到期由存储层自动删除，零运维满足 30 天上限。
optionExplanations_en: Storing everything forever and filtering in app code just rebuilds expiry logic the storage layer should own, plus constant table scans.
This denies the constraint entirely, but 30 days is exactly what the "no longer than necessary" requirement asks for.
Cold backup means keeping an extra copy, not deleting on schedule — it satisfies neither the storage goal nor the time limit.
Right: put a TTL on the rows and let the storage layer auto-delete at expiry, satisfying the 30-day cap with zero ops work.

q: 这几项被划出范围，分别让系统省掉了哪块设计？（多选）
q_en: For each item ruled out of scope, which piece of the design does it let you skip? (select all)
options: 不做音视频通话，就不用设计实时媒体流的中继/SFU 组件，Chat Server 只处理文本与附件元数据
不做商家交互，Chat/Message 实体就不用为「商业账号」单独设计消息模板或计费字段
不做注册与资料管理，User 实体就不用设计头像、简介变更的广播机制
既然通话不在范围内，实时收发消息也可以退回普通 HTTP 轮询，不必保留 WebSocket 长连接
options_en: Skipping calling means you never design a real-time media relay or SFU component; the Chat Server only handles text and attachment metadata
Skipping business interactions means Chat and Message never need a separate message template or billing field for business accounts
Skipping registration and profile management means the User entity never needs a broadcast mechanism for avatar or bio changes
Since calling is out of scope, real-time messaging can also fall back to plain HTTP polling instead of keeping a persistent WebSocket
why: 划出范围省掉的是那个功能自己的组件（SFU、商业消息模板、资料变更广播），不影响其他仍在范围内的需求；实时消息本身仍要求低延迟双向推送，跟通话是否在范围无关。
why_en: Ruling a feature out of scope only removes that feature's own component, not the messaging path, which still needs a persistent low-latency connection regardless of calling.
scenario: 面试官明确把音视频通话、商家/企业交互、注册与资料管理划到范围外，只保留群聊、收发消息、离线补投和媒体附件。
scenario_en: The interviewer explicitly puts audio/video calling, business interactions, and registration/profile management out of scope, keeping only group chat, messaging, offline delivery, and media attachments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 实时音视频通话里转发媒体流的服务器组件，只做转发不做混流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SFU is a server component in real-time calling that forwards media streams to participants without mixing them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

optionExplanations: 不做通话，Chat Server 就不用建 SFU 之类的实时媒体中继，只处理文本和附件元数据。
不做商家交互，Chat/Message 不用为商业账号单独设计模板或计费字段。
不做资料管理，User 实体不用为头像、简介变更设计广播机制。
实时收发消息本身仍要求低延迟双向推送，这条需求不因通话是否在范围而改变。
optionExplanations_en: Without calling, Chat Server never needs an SFU-style media relay — it only handles text and attachment metadata.
Without merchant interactions, Chat/Message never need business-account templates or billing fields.
Without profile management, User never needs a broadcast mechanism for avatar/bio changes.
Live send/receive still needs low-latency bidirectional push regardless of whether calling is in scope.

scenario: 非功能需求把「消息投递给在线用户」的延迟目标定在 500ms 以内。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirement sets a latency target of under five hundred milliseconds for delivering messages to online users.
q: 500ms 这个延迟目标，最直接把系统接口设计推向哪个方向？
q_en: Which direction does that five-hundred-millisecond latency target most directly push the interface design?
options: 客户端每 500ms 发一次 HTTP 轮询，查询是否有新消息
维持一条长连接（WebSocket），服务器直接把消息推给在线客户端
把消息统一批量打包，每隔几秒发送一次以节省带宽
延迟目标只影响 UI 动画速度，与传输方式无关
options_en: Have the client send an HTTP poll every 500ms to check for new messages
Keep a persistent connection (WebSocket) so the server can push messages straight to online clients
Batch messages together and send them out every few seconds to save bandwidth
The latency target only affects UI animation speed and has nothing to do with the transport
why: 500ms 排除了轮询间隔带来的延迟下限，只有服务器主动推送的长连接才能稳定达标。
why_en: A five-hundred-millisecond delivery target rules out polling-style delays and pushes the design toward a persistent connection that the server can push through immediately.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

optionExplanations: 轮询的延迟下限是轮询间隔本身，500ms 目标下很难稳定达标还浪费请求。
对：这个上限排除了轮询，服务器要主动把消息推给客户端才压得进去。
批量打包节省带宽，但引入的等待时间正好和延迟目标相反。
延迟目标决定的是投递路径要多快，不只是动画播放速度。
optionExplanations_en: Polling's latency floor is the poll interval itself — hard to hit 500ms reliably and it wastes requests.
Right: only a server-push long connection can reliably keep delivery under 500ms.
Batching saves bandwidth but adds waiting time, which works against a tight latency target.
The latency target constrains how fast the delivery path must be, not just how fast the UI animates.

scenario: 同一道 WhatsApp 设计题，只为会改变架构的非功能目标留时间，安全细节放 below the line。
scenario_en: Same WhatsApp design — you only budget time for the non-functional goals that actually change the architecture; security details go below the line.
q: 除了低延迟，本题的核心非功能需求还有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Besides low latency, which of these are also core non-functional requirements for this problem? (select all)
options: 详尽的安全与反爬虫防护
保证消息必达（deliverability）
支撑数十亿用户的高吞吐
消息在中心服务器保存不超过必要时长，且系统能抵御单组件故障
options_en: Exhaustive security and anti-scraping protections
Guaranteed deliverability of messages
High throughput to support billions of users
Messages stored no longer than necessary, with resilience to component failures
why: 核心 NFR：必达、数十亿用户高吞吐、消息不超期存储、组件级容错；安全细节与反爬虫被明确放到 below the line。
why_en: The core non-functional requirements are guaranteed deliverability, billions of users at high throughput, minimal server-side retention, and resilience to component failures, while deep security work is out of scope.
optionExplanations: 安全与反爬虫细节被明确放在 below the line，不是本题核心 NFR。
必达是核心 NFR：消息不能悄悄丢，这条约束贯穿 Inbox 和心跳设计。
数十亿用户的高吞吐是核心 NFR，决定了后面必须做水平扩展和分区路由。
保存期限和容错都是核心 NFR：既要按期清理，也要单组件故障不整体瘫痪。
optionExplanations_en: Security/anti-abuse detail is explicitly below the line, not a core NFR for this problem.
Deliverability is core — messages must not silently vanish, and it shapes both Inbox and heartbeat design.
High throughput at billions of users is core — it's why the design needs horizontal scaling and routing.
Retention limits and fault tolerance are both core — clean up on schedule, and no single component should take the system down.

scenario: WhatsApp 要同时支持 1:1 和最多 100 人群聊，你只想维护一套投递模型。
scenario_en: WhatsApp has to support both one-on-one chats and groups of up to a hundred, and you'd rather maintain a single delivery model.
q: 规划阶段关于 1:1 聊天与群聊的关键洞察是什么？
q_en: What is the key planning insight about one-on-one chat versus group chat?
options: 1:1 只是 2 人的群聊特例，按通用群聊模型处理
1:1 和群聊差异太大，必须两套独立系统
先只实现 1:1，群聊等以后重构
群聊可以用多次 1:1 发送来模拟
options_en: One-on-one chat is just the two-person special case, modeled with the general group-chat approach
One-on-one and group chat differ too much and need two separate systems
Build only one-on-one chat first and refactor in group chat later
Simulate a group chat by sending the same message one-on-one to each member
why: 把 1:1 看成 2 人的群聊，就能用一套通用模型覆盖两种场景；另一个规划洞察是把问题拆成「持久必达」和「实时投递」两部分。
why_en: One-on-one chats are just group chats with two participants, so the design solves the general group case while focusing on the dominant one-on-one traffic.
optionExplanations: 对：把 1:1 看成 2 人群聊，一套通用模型就能同时覆盖两种场景。
拆两套系统会让大量逻辑（成员、投递、Inbox）重复实现，规划阶段不必这样。
先做 1:1 再重构群聊，等于把群聊的扩展性问题留到后面才发现代价更高。
多次 1:1 发送模拟群聊会丢失「一条消息、一次投递事务」的语义，成员一致性也难保证。
optionExplanations_en: Right: treat 1:1 as a 2-person group and one general model covers both cases.
Splitting into two systems duplicates membership, delivery, and Inbox logic that a shared model already handles.
Building 1:1 first and refactoring group chat later means discovering the scaling cost only after the fact.
Simulating a group with repeated 1:1 sends loses the "one message, one delivery transaction" semantics and membership consistency.

q: 补全 WhatsApp 设计的四个核心实体：
q_en: Fill in the four core entities of the WhatsApp design:
text: 核心实体：{{User}}（用户）、{{Chat}}（2-100 人的会话）、{{Message}}（消息）、{{Client}}（同一用户可能有多台设备）。
why: Client 是同一账号下的一台已登录设备，不是泛泛前端代码。把 Client 和 User 分开，后面才能做多设备投递、per-client Inbox、ack 和重连 sync。
why_en: A Client is one logged-in device under a user, so separating it from User makes per-device delivery, ACKs, Inbox rows, and reconnect sync possible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 账号或人的身份，例如手机号、用户资料、账号级设置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A User is the account or person identity, such as phone number, profile, and account-level settings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一账号下的一台已登录设备或应用实例，例如手机、桌面端或网页端；它会有自己的连接、ack、sync 和待投递状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Client is one logged-in device or app instance under an account, such as phone, desktop, or web; it has its own connection, ACKs, sync state, and pending delivery state.

scenario: WhatsApp 用户常同时登录手机、平板和网页端，三端都要收到同一条消息并各自回 ack。
scenario_en: A WhatsApp user is often logged in on phone, tablet, and web at once, and all three have to get the message and ack separately.
q: 为什么实体里除了 User 还要单独定义 Client？
q_en: Why does the entity list define a separate Client alongside User?
options: 为了给每台设备单独计费
Client 只是 User 的别名，没有实际区别
为了做灰度实验分流
一个用户可能有多台设备，投递与同步要精确到设备
options_en: To bill each device separately
Client is just an alias for User with no real difference
To route users into A/B experiments
A user may own multiple devices, so delivery and sync must be tracked per device
why: User 是账号身份，Client 是这个账号下的一台已登录设备。多设备时每台设备的连接、lastSeq、ack 和 Inbox 都可能不同，所以投递与 sync 要按 client 跟踪。
why_en: User is the account, while Client is one logged-in device, so delivery, ACKs, last sequence, and Inbox state must be tracked per client in a multi-device design.
codeSample:
User:    userId = u123
Clients: phoneA, laptopB, webC

# 同一条消息发给 user u123 时，多设备要展开成多份待投递状态：
Inbox.put(clientId="phoneA",  messageId="m9")
Inbox.put(clientId="laptopB", messageId="m9")
Inbox.put(clientId="webC",    messageId="m9")

# phoneA ack 只清 phoneA/m9，不影响 laptopB 和 webC

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一账号下的一台已登录设备或应用实例，不是 User 的别名，也不只是前端代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Client is one logged-in device or app instance under an account; it is not an alias for User and not merely frontend code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 Client 当前连到 Chat Server 的活 WebSocket/TCP 连接；断线后 Client 还存在，但 Connection 不存在。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Connection is the live WebSocket/TCP connection from a Client to a Chat Server; after disconnect, the Client still exists but the Connection does not.

optionExplanations: 按设备计费不是这里要解决的问题，这道题考的是投递精度。
否认区别就等于回到单设备假设，多设备投递和 sync 就无从谈起。
灰度分流是运维手段，跟这里区分实体的目的无关。
对：一个账号可能有多台设备，投递与同步必须精确到设备而不是账号。
optionExplanations_en: Per-device billing isn't the problem being solved here — this is about delivery precision.
Denying the distinction collapses back to a single-device assumption, breaking multi-device delivery and sync.
Staged rollout is an ops concern, unrelated to why the entities are split here.
Right: one account can have multiple devices, so delivery and sync must track the device, not just the account.

scenario: 聊天应用里客户端要高频地发送消息，同时服务器要把别人发来的消息实时推给它——收发双向且频繁。
scenario_en: In a chat app the client sends messages frequently, and the server must also push other people's messages to it in real time — traffic is bidirectional and frequent.
q: 系统接口最合适的形态是？
q_en: What is the best shape for the system interface here?
options: REST + 客户端定时轮询
GraphQL 查询
双向 WebSocket 长连接，命令即 API
每条消息发起一个新的 HTTP 请求
options_en: REST with client-side polling on a timer
GraphQL queries
A bidirectional WebSocket connection, with commands acting as the API
A fresh HTTP request for every single message
why: 高频双向更新是双向 socket 的标准适用场景：客户端开 app 即建立连接，之后收发都以命令形式走这条连接。这是实时更新模式的典型应用。
why_en: High-frequency bidirectional updates are the perfect case for a persistent WebSocket connection that carries commands in both directions.
whenOtherWins: 普通「请求-响应」型产品用 REST 更合适；本设计里附件上传也刻意绕开 socket，走独立的 HTTP 服务。
tradeoff: 长连接双向实时推送 vs 简单请求-响应模型

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。

对：同样走加密的裸连接跑自定义协议，这条路径更贴近真实产品的落地方式。

q: 补全客户端发往服务器的四个核心命令：

scenario: WhatsApp 承诺 30 天内必达，服务器推完消息后要判断什么时候可以删掉 Inbox 那条记录。
scenario_en: WhatsApp guarantees delivery within thirty days, so after pushing a message the server has to decide when it may delete the Inbox row.
q: 客户端收到 newMessage 后必须回 ack，这一步换来了什么？
q_en: What does requiring the client to ack after receiving newMessage actually buy you?
options: 服务器确认送达客户端才清理 Inbox
客户端渲染速度更快
减少 WebSocket 握手次数
允许消息乱序到达
options_en: The server only clears the Inbox once it confirms the message reached the client
The client renders messages faster
It reduces the number of WebSocket handshakes
It allows messages to arrive out of order
why: 回执机制不起眼但至关重要：强制客户端 ack，服务器才有「消息已全程送达」的确定性，必达保证就建立在它之上。
why_en: Forcing clients to acknowledge receipt lets the server know a message truly reached the device, which is the foundation of guaranteed delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the confirmation signal a client sends back after receiving a message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

optionExplanations: 对：ack 让服务器拿到「客户端确实收到了」的确定性，才敢清理 Inbox 里的待投递记录。
渲染速度是客户端本地开销，跟服务器要不要收到确认信号无关。
ack 是应用层确认消息，不涉及握手次数，也不会减少它。
ack 恰恰是用来发现漏收、纠正顺序的信号，不是允许乱序的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the ack gives the server certainty the client actually received it, only then is it safe to clear the pending Inbox row.
Rendering speed is a client-local concern, unrelated to whether the server gets a confirmation signal.
The ack is an application-level confirmation; it doesn't touch WebSocket handshakes or reduce their count.
The ack is exactly the signal used to catch missed messages, not a license to tolerate out-of-order delivery.

scenario: Chat Server 走 WebSocket 长连接，不需要按路径或 Header 把流量路由到不同服务。
scenario_en: The Chat Server serves persistent WebSocket connections and never needs to route traffic to different services by path or header.
q: 负载均衡器应该怎么选？
q_en: Which load balancer should you pick here?
options: 必须 L7，因为它更「高级」
L4 就够：没有 L7 需求时性能更高
DNS 轮询即可，不需要 LB
客户端自己挑服务器
options_en: It must be L7 because L7 is "more advanced"
L4 is enough: without any L7 need, it performs better
Plain DNS round robin, no load balancer needed
Let the client pick a server itself
why: L4 只看 IP+端口，建连时挑一次后端就当哑管道转字节，正好配一直钉在同一台的 WebSocket。本题不按 path/header 分流，L7 终止 TLS、逐请求解析全是白干。
why_en: L4 only looks at IP and port: it picks a backend once at connect time and then forwards bytes like a dumb pipe, which suits a WebSocket pinned to one host. Nothing here routes by path or header, so L7's TLS termination and per-request parsing is wasted work.
whenOtherWins: 需要按 path/Header 把流量分到不同服务、改写 header、按 cookie 做会话粘性、或加 WAF 时，L7 才有价值。纯 WebSocket 长连接下 L7 在握手后也只是透传，几乎不比 L4 多做事却更贵。
tradeoff: L4 更高性能的直连转发 vs L7 按路径/Header 路由的灵活性

termDefinitions.meaning: 在传输层按 IP 和端口转发连接，不解析应用层内容，速度快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L4 load balancer forwards traffic at the transport layer using IP and port, without reading application data, which makes it fast.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在应用层解析请求内容（如路径、Header）后再决定路由，更灵活但更重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L7 load balancer reads application-layer data such as the path or headers before routing, which is more flexible but heavier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: LB 在自己这里把加密的 HTTPS/WSS 解密成明文，才能读到 HTTP 的 path/header 做路由(L7 必做)。代价是解密要花 CPU；L4 不解密、直接透传密文，所以更快但也看不到内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TLS termination: the LB decrypts encrypted HTTPS/WSS into plaintext so it can read the HTTP path/headers for routing (required for L7). It costs CPU to decrypt; L4 does not decrypt and passes the ciphertext straight through, so it is faster but blind to content.

termDefinitions.term: 按连接 vs 按请求
termDefinitions.meaning: L4 在「建立连接」时选一次后端，整条连接的字节都发去那台(长连接一直钉住)；L7 能在「每个 HTTP 请求」上重新选后端。长连接场景要的是前者——钉住同一台，因为 socket 只存在那台机器内存里。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L4 picks a backend once when the connection is established and all bytes go there (a long connection stays pinned); L7 can re-pick a backend for each HTTP request. Long-lived connections want the former — pinned to one host, because the socket lives only in that host memory.

optionExplanations: 选 L7 只因为它「听起来更高级」，不是基于本题实际需要的路由能力。
对：这里没有按路径/Header 路由的需求，L4 就够，且直连转发通常更快。
DNS 轮询不做健康检查也不管连接状态，撑不起长连接场景的容错。
客户端自选服务器意味着要把服务发现和健康状态暴露给客户端，责任放错了地方。
optionExplanations_en: Picking L7 just because it "sounds more advanced" isn't based on what this problem actually needs.
Right: there's no path/header routing need here, so L4 is enough and its direct forwarding is usually faster.
DNS round robin does no health checking or connection awareness, which isn't enough resilience for long-lived connections.
Letting the client pick its own server pushes service discovery and health state onto the client, the wrong place for that responsibility.
whenOtherWins_en: L7 pays off when you need path/header-based routing to different services, header rewriting, cookie-based session stickiness, or a WAF. For pure WebSocket connections L7 just passes through after the handshake — barely more than L4 but costlier.
codeSample:
# ===== L4 (AWS NLB / haproxy mode tcp) =====
listener:
  protocol: TCP            # 只认 TCP，不懂 HTTP、不解密 TLS
  port: 443
  backend_pool: chat_servers
  algorithm: least_connections   # 或 round_robin / hash(client_ip)
  health_check: { type: TCP, port: 443 }   # 只探端口通不通
# 没有 path/header 规则——L4 根本读不到应用层内容
#
# 行为：on new_tcp_conn -> backend = pool.pick(); pipe(client<->backend)
#       建连时选一次，之后纯转发字节，连接一直钉在同一后端(适配 WebSocket)

# ===== L7 (AWS ALB / nginx / haproxy mode http) =====
listener:
  protocol: HTTPS          # 终止 TLS：解密后才能读 HTTP
  port: 443
  tls_cert: chat.pem
  rules:                   # 按 HTTP 内容路由 = L7 唯一卖点
    - if path startsWith /chat  -> chat_servers
    - if path startsWith /media -> media_servers
    - default                   -> chat_servers
  sticky_session: { by: cookie }
  health_check: { type: HTTP, path: /healthz, expect: 200 }
#
# 行为：tls_decrypt(); for each http_request: parse; match_rule(path,header)
#       每个请求都可能路由到不同后端 —— 本题用不上，纯属多花 CPU/延迟

scenario: 在 DynamoDB 上建一个 100 人 WhatsApp 群，之后要能按会话查成员、也要能读会话元数据。
scenario_en: You create a hundred-person WhatsApp group on DynamoDB, and later you must be able to look up its members and read its metadata.
q: 处理 createChat 时服务端要写哪些记录？
q_en: Which records does the server write when handling createChat?
options: 只写一条 Chat 记录，参与者信息无处可查
只写 ChatParticipant 记录，会话没有名称、状态等元数据字段
先在 Message 表写一条占位消息，之后再回填成员
一条 Chat 加每人一条 ChatParticipant，小群一次事务，大群分批写
options_en: Write only one Chat record; there's nowhere to look up participant info
Write only ChatParticipant records; the chat itself has no name, status, or other metadata fields
Write a placeholder row into the Message table first and fill in members later
One Chat record plus one ChatParticipant per member; small groups in one transaction, large groups batched
why: createChat 要同时写会话元数据和成员边：1 条 Chat 存 type/name/status，N 条 ChatParticipant 存成员。小群可事务写；大群超 DynamoDB 单事务上限要分批，靠状态或幂等重试兜住半完成。
why_en: createChat writes one Chat row for conversation metadata and one ChatParticipant row per member; small groups fit in one transaction, while 100-person groups may need batched idempotent creation.
diagram:
flowchart TD A[Client calls createChat
participants = u1,u2,u3] --> B[Create Chat row
chatId, type, name, createdAt, status] B --> C[Create ChatParticipant rows] C --> C1[chatId#u1] C --> C2[chatId#u2] C --> C3[chatId#u3] C --> D[Return chatId] D --> E[Later sendMessage queries
ChatParticipant by chatId]
codeSample:
createChat(creatorId, participantIds, name=None):
  chatId = newULID()
  members = unique(participantIds + [creatorId])

  chat = {
    "PK": chatId,
    "type": "GROUP" if len(members) > 2 else "DM",
    "name": name,
    "createdBy": creatorId,
    "createdAt": now(),
    "status": "ACTIVE"
  }

  participantRows = [
    {
      "PK": chatId,
      "SK": userId,
      "role": "ADMIN" if userId == creatorId else "MEMBER",
      "joinedAt": now(),
      "lastReadSeq": 0,
      "mute": False
    }
    for userId in members
  ]

  if 1 + len(participantRows) <= 100:
    transactWrite([chat] + participantRows)  # all-or-nothing
  else:
    put(chat with status="CREATING")
    batchWrite(participantRows)              # chunked/idempotent
    update(chatId, status="ACTIVE")

  return chatId

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。

termDefinitions.meaning: 创建一个会话容器的服务端命令，不是发送消息。它会生成 chatId，写会话元数据和成员关系，然后把 chatId 返回给客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: createChat is the server command that creates a conversation container, not a message send. It generates a chatId, writes conversation metadata and membership rows, and returns the chatId to the client.

termDefinitions.meaning: 会话本身的记录，保存 chatId、类型、名称、创建者、创建时间、状态等会话级元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Chat is the conversation-level record storing chatId, type, name, creator, creation time, status, and other conversation metadata.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录某个会话里都有哪些成员的关联表；通常一人一行，也可以保存 role、joinedAt、lastReadSeq、mute 等成员级字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ChatParticipant is the membership table recording which members belong to a chat; it is usually one row per member and can store role, joinedAt, lastReadSeq, mute, and other member-level fields.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多条写入当成一个原子操作：全部成功才算成功，任何一条失败就整体回滚。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction treats multiple writes as one atomic operation: all writes succeed together, or the whole operation rolls back.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次写不下太多记录时，把记录拆成多个批次写入。它通常不是一个全局原子事务，所以要配合幂等 key 和状态字段处理重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batched writes split a large set of rows into multiple write batches. They are usually not one global atomic transaction, so idempotent keys and status fields are used to handle retries.

optionExplanations: 只有 Chat 元数据，成员这条边完全没落地，查不出谁在会话里。
只有成员边，会话本身缺少名称、状态这类描述信息，等于没有可展示的会话对象。
Message 表是消息正文的地盘，用它占位存成员，混淆了两张表各自的职责。
对：一条记录描述会话本身，另一批记录各描述一个成员，小群一次提交、大群才分批写。
optionExplanations_en: Only the Chat row exists — the membership edge is missing, so no one can be looked up as a participant.
Only membership rows exist — the chat itself has no type/name/status, so there's no displayable chat object.
The Message table owns message bodies; using it as a member placeholder confuses what each table is for.
Right: one Chat row for the chat itself, one ChatParticipant row per member; small groups write in one transaction, large groups batch.

scenario: WhatsApp 的 Chat 表在 DynamoDB 上只有一种访问模式：按 chatId 读这个会话的详情。
scenario_en: The WhatsApp Chat table on DynamoDB has exactly one access pattern: read a chat's details by chatId.
q: Chat 表的主键怎么设计？
q_en: How should the Chat table's primary key be designed?
options: chatId + createdAt 复合主键
participantId 作主键
chatId 简单主键即可——通常只按会话 ID 查详情
会话名称作主键
options_en: A composite key of chatId plus createdAt
participantId as the primary key
A simple primary key on chatId is enough, since lookups are almost always by chat id
The chat name as the primary key
why: Chat 表的访问模式就是按 chatId 取详情，简单主键足够；复杂的查询需求都落在 ChatParticipant 表上。
why_en: The chat table only needs a simple primary key on the chat id because lookups are always by id.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行数据被分配到哪个物理分区的键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which physical partition a row of data lands on.

optionExplanations: 复合键暗示还要按 createdAt 查会话，但访问模式只有按 chatId 查一条。
participantId 是成员维度的键，不该出现在描述会话本身的 Chat 表里。
对：这张表唯一的查法是给一个 ID 就要回详情，不需要额外维度参与定位。
会话名可重复、可修改，不满足主键唯一且稳定的要求。
optionExplanations_en: A composite key implies querying by createdAt too, but the access pattern is just a single lookup by chatId.
participantId is a membership-level key; it doesn't belong on the Chat table, which describes the chat itself.
Right: the access pattern is a lookup by chatId, so a simple primary key is enough — no composite needed.

scenario: 打开一个 100 人 WhatsApp 群时要立刻列出全部成员，这一步只能花一次 DynamoDB 查询。

scenario: 单台 Chat Server 要在毫秒内把消息 push 进接收者那条已经建好的 WebSocket。
scenario_en: A single Chat Server has to push a message into the recipient's already-open WebSocket within milliseconds.
q: 单机 Chat Server 用什么追踪「谁连着我」？
q_en: What does a single-host Chat Server use to track who is currently connected?
options: 每次去数据库查连接表
Redis 里存一个全局在线集合
内存哈希表：userId 映射连接对象
写文件日志再解析
options_en: Query a connections table in the database on every send
Keep a global set of online users in Redis
An in-process hash map mapping userId to its WebSocket connection
Write to a log file and parse it back
why: 要 push 就得握着那条活的 WebSocket——它是进程内存里的句柄，序列化不进 Redis。单机一张 userId 到 socket 的内存表就够，跨机路由才另加 Redis presence。
why_en: Pushing a message means holding the live WebSocket, and that handle lives in process memory — you cannot serialize it into Redis. One host needs only an in-memory userId-to-socket map; Redis presence comes in later, just for cross-host routing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: 运行时里的 socket/连接句柄，代表一条已经建立的网络连接；它绑定在接收连接的进程内，不能像普通字符串一样存进 Redis。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection object is a runtime socket handle for an established network connection; it is owned by the process that accepted it and cannot be stored in Redis like a string.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨服务器保存 userId 当前在哪台 Chat Server 上的轻量索引；它能帮忙路由，但不是连接本体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A presence index records which Chat Server currently owns a user; it helps route messages but is not the connection itself.

termDefinitions.term: 本机内存 vs 外部内存存储
termDefinitions.fullName: in-process heap vs external in-memory store
termDefinitions.meaning: 「内存」有两义:①本机进程内存=你 Chat Server 进程自己的 heap，装活的语言对象(socket/句柄/线程)，指针解引用(纳秒)，只有本进程可见、进程死即失。②外部内存存储(Redis/Memcached)=另一个进程/机器的 RAM，走网络访问(亚毫秒，慢~1000×)，只能装序列化字节、跨服务器共享、进程重启仍在。Redis/Memcached 也是「in-memory」，但指它们自己把数据放 RAM，不等于你进程的 heap。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: "In memory" has two senses: (1) in-process heap = your Chat Server process's own heap, holding live language objects (sockets/handles/threads), accessed by pointer deref (ns), visible only to this process, lost when it dies; (2) external in-memory store (Redis/Memcached) = another process/machine's RAM, accessed over the network (sub-ms, ~1000× slower), holding only serialized bytes, shared across servers, surviving app restarts. Redis/Memcached are "in-memory" meaning they keep their data in RAM — not the same as your process heap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 都是外部内存 KV，都装不了活 socket。Memcached:只存字符串/blob、多线程、无持久化、无 pub/sub，极简纯缓存。Redis:富数据结构(list/set/hash/zset)+pub/sub+持久化(RDB/AOF)，是「数据结构服务器」。WhatsApp 用 Redis 做 presence+pub/sub 路由，正因为需要 pub/sub 和数据结构——Memcached 做不了 pub/sub。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Both are external in-memory KV stores and neither can hold a live socket. Memcached: strings/blobs only, multi-threaded, no persistence, no pub/sub — a minimal pure cache. Redis: rich data structures (list/set/hash/zset) + pub/sub + persistence (RDB/AOF), a "data-structure server". WhatsApp uses Redis for presence + pub/sub routing precisely because it needs pub/sub and data structures — Memcached cannot do pub/sub.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条连接 = socket 文件描述符(fd)+内核 TCP 状态+应用层缓冲，全绑在接住它的那个进程里，是指向活内核资源的句柄。fd 号在别的进程无意义、内核状态不可转移，所以序列化不了、搬不走。要给客户端发字节必须在拥有该 fd 的进程里调 send()——因此连接只能存本机 heap，Redis/Memcached/DB 都装不了，它们只能存「人在哪台服务器」的路由字节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A connection = a socket file descriptor (fd) + kernel TCP state + app-layer buffers, all bound to the process that accepted it — a handle to a live kernel resource. The fd number is meaningless in another process and the kernel state is not transferable, so it cannot be serialized or moved. Sending bytes to the client requires calling send() from the process owning that fd — so a connection lives only in local heap; Redis/Memcached/DB can hold only the routing bytes of "which server the user is on".

optionExplanations: 每次发消息都查库，既慢又没必要——连接状态是高频读的内存态数据。
全局在线集合能答「谁在线」，但装不下 socket 对象；多机时它的正确角色是 presence 路由。
对：只有本机进程内存能持有真实的 socket 对象，查表即可直接写回该连接。
写文件日志再解析拿不到实时可用的连接对象，只能做事后分析。
optionExplanations_en: Querying the database on every send is slow and unnecessary — connection state is hot, in-memory data.
A global online set can answer who is online, but it cannot hold a socket object; across hosts its real job is presence routing.
Right — only this process's own memory can hold the real socket object, so a map lookup gets you straight to the connection.
Writing a log file and parsing it never yields a live, usable connection object — only after-the-fact analysis.
whenOtherWins: 横向扩到多台 Chat Server 时才加 Redis：它当 presence index(userId→哪台服务器)用于跨机路由，不替代本地内存表——真 socket 永远只在本机内存里。触发点是「多台服务器」而非「多台设备」，单台服务器可在一个内存表里握住海量设备连接。
whenOtherWins_en: Redis enters only when scaling to multiple Chat Servers: it acts as a presence index (userId→which server) for cross-host routing, never replacing the local map — the real socket always lives only in that host's memory. The trigger is many servers, not many devices; one server holds a huge number of device connections in a single map.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。

It assumes every user is connected to the same Chat Server — that gets broken by multi-machine Pub/Sub routing.
It assumes the connection always works — that gets broken by heartbeats and stale-connection detection.

scenario: 用户离线时发给他的消息，30 天内重新上线必须能收到；在线用户则要即时收到。
scenario_en: A message sent to an offline user must still be delivered if they reconnect within thirty days, while online users need it delivered immediately.
q: 文中的存储设计是？
q_en: What is the article's storage design for this?
options: 完全依赖客户端本地存储互相同步
每个接收者有 Inbox：在线即时投递，离线等回来补发
把离线消息转成推送通知即可
为每个用户建一个 Kafka topic 当收件箱
options_en: Rely entirely on client-side local storage syncing with each other
Each recipient gets an inbox: deliver immediately if online, or wait for reconnect if offline
Just convert offline messages into push notifications
Create one Kafka topic per user as their inbox
why: Inbox 是必达与离线支持的核心：先写库再投递，ack 后删除。它把「持久必达」与「实时投递」解耦成两条路径。
why_en: Each recipient gets an inbox of undelivered messages that is written before any delivery attempt and cleared only after the client acknowledges.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品只服务在线场景（比如直播弹幕），不需要 Inbox，直接经连接推送、丢了就丢了。
tradeoff: 持久 Inbox 保证离线必达 vs 只走实时推送的简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息持久化到磁盘、按 topic 组织、并维护消费者位点的分布式消息队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue that persists messages to disk, organizes them into topics, and tracks consumer offsets.

optionExplanations: 纯客户端互相同步没有中心事实源，多设备和离线一致性都无法保证。
对：Inbox 把「持久必达」和「实时投递」解耦——在线即时推，离线等回来 sync。
直接转推送通知丢失了消息正文本身的可靠存储，通知被划走也就永久漏收。
每用户一个 Kafka topic 的元数据开销和 Inbox 的精确查询需求不匹配，这不是这里的存储设计。
optionExplanations_en: Pure client-to-client sync has no central source of truth, so multi-device and offline consistency can't be guaranteed.
Right: an Inbox decouples "must eventually deliver" from "deliver live" — instant push online, sync on reconnect offline.
Converting straight to a push notification drops reliable storage of the message body — dismiss the notification and it's gone for good.
A Kafka topic per user carries metadata overhead that doesn't match what an Inbox needs to query precisely — that's not this design.

scenario: 群聊里接收者可能离线，也可能 Chat Server 在实时推送前崩溃；这题考的是先把“必须投递给谁”落到可靠存储。
scenario_en: In a group chat a recipient may be offline, or the Chat Server could crash before the real-time push; this card tests durably recording who still needs delivery before anything else.
q: 把「发送一条消息」的完整流程排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the full flow of sending a message into the correct order:
steps: Chat Server 写 Message 表 + 为每个接收者创建 Inbox 条目（持久化）
发送者经 WebSocket 发出 sendMessage
Chat Server 尝试经各在线参与者的连接实时投递 newMessage
Chat Server 查 ChatParticipant 表得到全部参与者
已连接客户端回 ack，服务器从 Inbox 删除该消息
向发送者返回 SUCCESS 和最终 messageId
why: 先写 Inbox，是为了先落下“谁还没收到”的债务。Message 存正文，Inbox 存每个接收者的待投递指针；实时 WebSocket 只是加速路径，ack 后才清理。
why_en: Write the inbox before realtime push so delivery obligation is durable. The message table stores the body once. Inbox rows store per-recipient pending delivery state. Realtime WebSocket push is a fast path. If the server crashes before push, recipients can replay from the inbox after reconnect. Delete or mark an inbox row only after that recipient ACKs.
tradeoff: 可靠投递优先 vs 在线用户即时推送；多写一份 Inbox 换来离线补拉和崩溃恢复
diagram:
sequenceDiagram

    participant CS as Chat Server
    participant DB as DynamoDB
    participant R as 接收者
    S->>CS: sendMessage
    CS->>DB: 查 ChatParticipant
    CS->>DB: 写 Message + Inbox（持久化）
    CS-->>S: SUCCESS + messageId
    CS->>R: newMessage（尽力而为）
    R-->>CS: ack
    CS->>DB: 删除 Inbox 条目

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。它不是内存列表，而是数据库里的待投递记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient delivery queue stored in a database, not just an in-memory list.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据写到数据库或日志里。进程重启后，数据仍然能被读回来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability means writing data to storage such as a database or log so it survives process restarts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 会话成员表。Chat Server 用它找出这条消息应该投递给哪些用户。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ChatParticipant is the membership table that tells the server which users should receive a message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the confirmation signal a client sends back after receiving a message.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

scenario: WhatsApp 类聊天里，用户离线时服务器可能已经把消息写入数据库，但实时 WebSocket 投递没有成功。客户端重新连上后，系统要补发这位用户还没确认收到的消息。
scenario_en: In a WhatsApp-like chat system, messages may already be persisted while realtime WebSocket delivery failed because the user was offline. When the client reconnects, the system needs to redeliver only the messages that this user has not acknowledged.
q: 离线客户端重新连接后的补发流程是？
q_en: What is the redelivery flow when an offline client reconnects?
options: 无差别重发最近 24 小时的全部消息，浪费带宽也不精确
客户端自己去扫 Message 表，既没权限也没索引
查 Inbox 拿未投递 ID，取消息体下发，ack 后删除
等下一条新消息到来时顺带同步，安静期会一直漏
options_en: Blindly resend every message from the last 24 hours, wasting bandwidth and imprecise
Have the client scan the Message table itself, with neither the permission nor the index to do so
Read the Inbox for undelivered ids, fetch each body, deliver, then delete after ack
Wait until the next new message arrives and piggyback a sync then, missing everything during a quiet period
why: 离线补发查的是未完成投递，不是全量历史。客户端重连后 sync，服务端按 userId/clientId 查 PENDING Inbox，取 Message 正文下发；客户端幂等保存并 ack 后才清理。
why_en: Reconnect sync queries pending Inbox rows by userId or clientId, fetches Message bodies, sends them down, and clears them only after the client stores and ACKs them.
whenOtherWins: 低价值提醒或弹幕可以丢，重连拉最新状态即可，不必维护 Inbox。
tradeoff: 精确可靠补发 vs 多写一份 per-recipient Inbox
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant CS as Chat Server
    participant I as Inbox
    participant M as Message table
    C->>CS: reconnect + auth
    C->>CS: sync(clientId/userId)
    CS->>I: query pending messageIds
    I-->>CS: m123, m124
    CS->>M: fetch message bodies
    M-->>CS: message bodies
    CS-->>C: deliver over WebSocket
    C-->>CS: ack(messageId)
    CS->>I: delete or mark delivered
codeSample:
Inbox row:
  PK = clientId
  SK = createdAt#messageId
  chatId = chat123
  messageId = msg789
  status = PENDING

onWebSocketOpen():
  send({ type: "sync", clientId, userId })

handleSync(clientId):
  rows = inbox.query(clientId, status="PENDING", limit=100)
  messages = messageTable.batchGet(rows.map(r => r.messageId))
  websocket.send({ type: "syncMessages", messages })  # each message includes chatId

onClientReceive(message):
  localStore.upsert(message.chatId, message.id, message)  # idempotent
  send({ type: "ack", messageId: message.id })

handleAck(clientId, messageId):
  inbox.delete(clientId, messageId)  # or mark DELIVERED

rows: 正文按会话顺序存一次

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户重连后，服务器把这位用户尚未确认收到的消息重新投递一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offline redelivery means sending messages again after reconnect when this user has not acknowledged them yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列，通常按接收者/client 查询，但 row 里仍可带 messageId、chatId、createdAt、status 等属性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of undelivered messages. It is usually queried by recipient/client, but each row can still contain attributes such as messageId, chatId, createdAt, and status.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保存消息正文和元数据的主表；Inbox 指向它，避免给每个接收者复制正文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Message table stores message body and metadata; inbox rows point to it instead of copying the body per recipient.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息所属会话的 ID。它可以直接存在 Inbox row 里，也可以作为 Message 表里的字段通过 messageId 读出来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: chatId is the id of the conversation that owns the message. It can be stored directly on the inbox row, or fetched from the Message table by messageId.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the confirmation signal a client sends back after receiving a message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端在重连、回到前台或定时兜底时向服务器请求未收到消息；不是扫全量历史，而是让服务端查 Inbox 的待投递记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sync is the client asking the server for messages it has not received after reconnect, foregrounding, or a periodic backstop; it is not a full history scan, but a server-side Inbox replay.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一台具体设备或客户端实例的 ID。多设备聊天里通常按 clientId 维护 Inbox，避免手机 ack 后电脑漏收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A clientId identifies one device or client instance. In multi-device chat, the Inbox is often keyed by clientId so one device's ACK does not hide messages from another device.

optionExplanations: 无差别重发固定窗口既浪费带宽又不精确——有些漏的消息可能更早，有些根本没漏。
客户端没有权限也没索引直接扫 Message 表，这条路径在权限模型上就走不通。
对：查 Inbox 拿到未投递的消息 ID，取正文下发，客户端 ack 后才清理，精确又不重扫。
等下一条消息顺带同步意味着安静期内漏掉的消息永远没有触发点，会一直漏下去。
optionExplanations_en: Blindly resending a fixed time window wastes bandwidth and is imprecise — some misses are older, some were never missed at all.
The client has neither permission nor an index to scan the Message table directly — this path fails on the permission model alone.
Right: query the Inbox for undelivered message IDs, fetch the bodies, and clear them only after the client acks — precise, no blind scanning.
Piggybacking on the next new message means a quiet period with no new traffic never triggers a sync, so the gap never gets caught.

scenario: Inbox 与 Message 表里超过 30 天的旧数据需要定期清理，既控制存储也满足「保存不超必要时长」。
scenario_en: Rows older than thirty days in the Inbox and Message tables need periodic cleanup, both to control storage and to satisfy the "no longer than necessary" requirement.
q: 最省事的清理机制是？
q_en: What is the least effort way to handle this cleanup?
options: 每天跑全表扫描批量删除
给条目设 TTL，到期自动删除
依赖客户端发起删除请求
写个 cron 脚本逐行比对时间戳
options_en: Run a full table scan every day and batch-delete
Set a TTL on the entries and let them expire automatically
Rely on the client to send a delete request
Write a cron script that compares timestamps row by row
why: 给条目设 TTL 让存储层自动过期，零运维成本地满足 30 天上限；这与附件存储的 30 天 TTL 是同一思路。
why_en: Setting a time-to-live on the inbox and message items lets the store expire old rows automatically and honors the thirty-day retention limit.
whenOtherWins: 若业务要求永久聊天历史（云端全量同步类产品），TTL 删除就不适用，需要专门的归档与分层存储。
tradeoff: TTL 自动过期的零运维 vs 定时任务人工可控的清理节奏

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储条目设置的存活期限，到期后由存储层自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TTL is an expiration time after which the storage layer automatically deletes the item.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

optionExplanations: 全表扫描要遍历所有条目再挑出过期的，成本随数据量增长，还得自己调度。
对：给条目设 TTL，存储层到点自动删除，零运维满足 30 天上限。
依赖客户端主动删除意味着客户端不发请求，过期数据就一直留着。
cron 脚本逐行比对时间戳本质是自建了一遍存储层已经提供的能力，多余的运维负担。
optionExplanations_en: A full scan has to walk every row to find expired ones — cost grows with data size and still needs manual scheduling.
Right: put a TTL on the rows and the storage layer auto-deletes at expiry — zero ops to satisfy the 30-day cap.
Relying on the client to request deletion means expired data just sits there if the client never asks.
A cron job comparing timestamps row by row re-implements a capability the storage layer already offers, adding needless ops work.

scenario: 2 亿活跃用户，人均每天约发送 20 条消息。
scenario_en: There are two hundred million active users, each sending about twenty messages a day on average.
q: 由此估算出的发送速率量级，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Which conclusion does the resulting send-rate estimate most directly support?
options: 算下来每天约 4 亿条、峰值也就百来条/秒，随便一台单机数据库都扛得住
算下来每天约 40 亿条、约 4 万条/秒，已超单机数据库范围，写入要走水平扩展存储
算出来的数字大到荒谬，说明这类估算在面试里没有意义
算下来约 400 万条/秒，逼近现有任何存储方案的物理极限，必须自建存储引擎
options_en: About 400M/day, peak only around a hundred/sec — any single-machine database handles that fine
About 4B/day, roughly 40k/sec — already beyond single-machine range, writes need horizontally scalable storage
The resulting number is absurdly large, meaning this kind of estimation is pointless in interviews
About 4M/sec, pushing the physical limit of any storage option, requiring a custom-built storage engine
why: messages/s = 2 亿 × 20 ÷ 86,400 ≈ 46k，面试按 4-5 万/秒说。锚点是单库持久化写入约 1 万/秒，高出 5~10 倍，所以写入必须水平分区。
why_en: Messages per second equals 200 million times 20 divided by 86,400, about 46k, which you'd quote as forty to fifty thousand a second. The peg is that one database does roughly ten thousand durable writes a second, so at five to ten times that you have to partition writes horizontally.
diagram:
flowchart LR A[200M active users] --> C[4B messages/day] B[20 messages/user/day] --> C C --> D[Divide by 86,400 sec/day] D --> E[~46k messages/s
round to ~40k-50k]
codeSample:
active_users = 200_000_000
messages_per_user_per_day = 20
seconds_per_day = 24 * 60 * 60  # 86,400

messages_per_day = active_users * messages_per_user_per_day
# 200M * 20 = 4B messages/day

messages_per_sec = messages_per_day / seconds_per_day
# 4B / 86,400 ~= 46k messages/s
# interview answer: about 40k-50k messages/s

rows: 单 WebSocket 服务器连接数
~10 万 ~ 百万连接(内存/fd 限)

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒用户发出的逻辑消息数量。它是原始发送速率，不等于数据库写入次数；一条消息后面可能写 Message、Inbox，群聊还会 fan-out。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Messages per second is the number of logical user-sent messages per second. It is the raw send rate, not the database write rate; one message can later create Message rows, Inbox rows, and group fan-out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一天的总量平均摊到 86,400 秒得到的速率。真实系统还要考虑峰值，通常再乘一个 peak factor。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Average rate means spreading the daily total across 86,400 seconds. A real system also considers peak traffic, usually by multiplying by a peak factor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 峰值流量相对平均流量的倍数。面试第一步常先算平均量级，再说明生产容量要按峰值冗余规划。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A peak factor is the multiplier between peak traffic and average traffic. In interviews, first estimate the average order of magnitude, then mention that production capacity needs peak headroom.

termDefinitions.meaning: 经验锚点:单个关系库节点的可靠(带 fsync/事务)写入约几千~1 万/秒(量级 10⁴)。因为每条写要 WAL 刷盘(受磁盘 IOPS 限)+更新索引+常等副本 ack，再叠单写入者锁竞争。读便宜得多(靠缓存可达 10⁵+)，所以瓶颈几乎总是写。数字随硬件/配置浮动，面试用「单节点~1 万写/秒」当锚点最稳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rule-of-thumb peg: a single relational DB node sustains ~a few thousand to ~10k durable (fsync/transactional) writes/s (order 10^4), because each write needs a WAL fsync (disk-IOPS bound) + index updates + often a replica ack, plus single-writer lock contention. Reads are far cheaper (10^5+ via cache), so writes are almost always the bottleneck. It varies with hardware/config; "~10k writes/s per node" is the safest interview anchor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 容量估算只需算对「10 的几次方」，不必精确。判断「是否超单机」就是比量级:发送 4-5 万/秒(10⁴·几倍) vs 单库写 ~1 万/秒(10⁴) → 超了要分片。考官看的是你能不能用锚点(单机写~10⁴、缓存读~10⁵)迅速定位瓶颈，而非小数点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Capacity estimation only needs the right power of ten, not precision. Deciding "exceeds one machine" is a magnitude comparison: 46k/s send (a few × 10^4) vs ~10k/s single-node writes (10^4) → exceeds, so shard. Interviewers watch whether you locate the bottleneck fast using anchors (single-node writes ~10^4, cached reads ~10^5), not the decimals.

optionExplanations: 每日消息数少算了一位（漏乘或算错单位），得出的百来条/秒严重低估真实压力。
对：约 4-5 万条/秒已越过单机数据库的耐久写能力，存储层必须横向铺开。
估算结果本身没有荒谬——4-5 万/秒是可信量级，面试就靠这类粗算判断方向。
多算了近百倍，把发送速率和真实写入量级搞混，结论过度悲观。
optionExplanations_en: The daily count is off by an order of magnitude (a mis-multiplied unit), so the resulting hundred/sec badly underestimates real load.
Right — roughly forty to fifty thousand a second is past what one database can durably absorb, so storage has to spread out horizontally.
The result isn't absurd — 40-50k/sec is a believable order of magnitude, exactly the kind of back-of-envelope math interviews expect.
This overshoots by nearly 100x, conflating send rate with real write volume and landing on an overly pessimistic conclusion.

scenario: 在上一步估算的发送速率基础上，每条 1:1 消息要写一次 Message、一次接收者 Inbox，再叠加群聊的多接收者放大。
scenario_en: Building on the previous send-rate estimate, every one-on-one message writes once to Message and once to the recipient's Inbox, plus the extra fan-out from group chats.
q: 算上双写与群聊放大后的总写入量级，最支持哪个结论？
q_en: Counting the double write and the group fan-out, which conclusion does the total write-rate estimate support?
options: 总写入量级冲到约 1000 万/秒，DynamoDB 撑不住，必须自研存储引擎
双写和群聊放大可以忽略不计，量级和单条发送速率一样
这类估算不可靠，唯一办法是直接上生产环境压测
总写入约 10 万/秒——水平分区 KV/NoSQL 可作候选，不必仅因此自研存储
options_en: Total write volume spikes to about 10M/sec, DynamoDB can't handle it, so a custom storage engine is required
Double-writes and group fan-out are negligible, so the volume equals the raw send rate
This kind of estimation is unreliable; the only real option is load-testing in production
Total writes land around 100k/sec — a horizontally partitioned KV/NoSQL store can be a candidate, not a forced custom build
why: 写入量 ≈ 原始发送速率 × 每条写入行数：1:1 是 Message+Inbox≈2 行，群聊按平均接收者放大，约 4 万×2.5≈10 万 writes/s。结论是可选水平分区 KV/NoSQL，不是单表单区无峰值地扛完整产品。
why_en: Storage writes are raw sends times rows per message: Message plus Inbox is about two writes for 1:1, and average group fan-out brings the estimate near 100k writes/s.

rows: 不是所有消息都只 2 次写
按平均接收者数估写放大
不是都按 100 人上限算
水平分区 KV/NoSQL 可候选
不是单表单区域能撑全部
不是说必须用 AWS DynamoDB

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。这里它是“水平分区 KV/NoSQL 存储”的代表，不等于一台数据库机器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key. Here it stands for a horizontally partitioned KV/NoSQL store, not one database machine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里常用来泛指按 key 水平扩展、托管容量、自动分区的 KV/NoSQL 存储。也可以替换成 Cassandra、Bigtable、ScyllaDB 或公司内部类似系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DynamoDB-style store is interview shorthand for a key-partitioned, horizontally scalable KV/NoSQL store with managed or distributed capacity. Cassandra, Bigtable, ScyllaDB, or an internal equivalent could play a similar role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个分区键承载过多读写，导致单个分区先成为瓶颈。即使用 DynamoDB/Cassandra，也要避免极热 userId、chatId 或时间桶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot partition happens when one partition key receives too much traffic and becomes a bottleneck. Even with DynamoDB or Cassandra, very hot userId, chatId, or time-bucket keys need mitigation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条写入或消息被放大成多条下游操作的过程，例如一条群消息要分发给每个成员。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is when a single write or message multiplies into many downstream operations, like delivering one group message to every member.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个用户动作在存储层变成多次写入。这里一条消息至少写 Message + Inbox 两类记录，群聊还会按接收者数继续放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification means one user action turns into multiple storage writes. Here one message writes at least Message plus Inbox records, and group chats amplify further by recipient count.

termDefinitions.meaning: 容量估算里用的平均 fan-out。100 人群是上限/尾部，不代表每条消息都要乘 100。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Average recipient count is the fan-out used for capacity estimates. A one-hundred-person group is an upper bound or tail case, not a multiplier for every message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 保存消息正文、发送者、会话和时间等元数据的主记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Message record stores the body, sender, chat, timestamp, and related metadata for one message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户标识，作为分区键时会把不同用户的收件箱写入分散到不同分区。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A userId is the user identifier; as a partition key, it spreads inbox writes across users.

optionExplanations: 把发送速率和写入行数的乘数算大了近百倍，结论过度悲观，不符合估算过程。
双写（Message+Inbox）和群聊放大都是真实倍数，忽略它们会低估实际写入压力。
估算本身就是面试的一部分，能给出量级和判断方向，不代表要靠它替代压测。
对：约 4 万发送/秒 × 平均约 2.5 次写 ≈ 10 万 writes/秒，落在水平分区 KV/NoSQL 的合理候选范围。
optionExplanations_en: This multiplies send rate by write count nearly 100x too high, landing on an overly pessimistic conclusion that doesn't match the math.
Double-writes (Message+Inbox) and group fan-out are both real multipliers; ignoring them understates the actual write pressure.
Estimation is itself part of the interview — it gives an order of magnitude and direction, not a substitute for load testing.
Right: roughly 40k sends/sec × ~2.5 writes each ≈ 100k writes/sec, squarely in range for a horizontally partitioned KV/NoSQL candidate.

scenario: WhatsApp 要支持发图片和视频，单个附件上百 MB，而 Chat Server 同时扛着实时消息推送。
scenario_en: WhatsApp has to carry photos and videos of hundreds of megabytes while the Chat Server is also pushing real-time messages.
q: 把附件二进制直接存进数据库（经 WebSocket 上传）有哪两个核心问题？
q_en: What are the two core problems with uploading attachment bytes through WebSocket and storing them directly in the database?
options: 成本太低不划算，其实存储成本不是这里的瓶颈
事务冲突太多，其实这不是并发写入的问题
数据库不擅长大二进制 blob，且拖累 Chat Server 带宽
无法给附件设 TTL 到期删除，其实 TTL 这类过期机制一直可以设置
options_en: Storage cost is too low to matter, but storage cost is not the real bottleneck here
Too many transaction conflicts, but this is not actually a concurrent-write problem
The database is a poor fit for large blobs, and the path consumes Chat Server bandwidth
Attachments cannot get a TTL for automatic cleanup, but expiration can still be configured
why: 大 blob 会放大数据库 I/O、备份和查询开销；媒体字节经 Chat Server/WebSocket 转发，还会抢走实时消息带宽。附件应该进专用 blob 存储，数据库只留元数据。
why_en: Large blobs inflate database I/O and backups, and routing media through Chat Server burns bandwidth that should stay reserved for realtime messages.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C[Client] -->|media bytes over WebSocket| CS[Chat Server]
    CS -->|large blob bytes| DB[(Database)]
    C -. preferred bytes .-> BS[(Blob storage)]
    CS -. metadata only .-> DB

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器之间保持的一条双向长连接，适合聊天事件和小消息，不适合搬运大媒体字节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a long-lived bidirectional connection between client and server; it fits chat events and small messages, not large media bytes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护用户长连接并收发聊天事件的服务；让它转发媒体会挤占消息投递的 CPU 和网络预算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Chat Server holds user connections and chat events; making it relay media consumes CPU and network budget needed for message delivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大二进制对象，例如图片、语音或视频附件；通常放进对象/blob 存储，而不是主业务数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A blob is a large binary object such as an image, voice note, or video attachment; it usually belongs in object/blob storage, not the main database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储条目设置的存活期限，到期后由存储层自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TTL is an expiration time after which the storage layer automatically deletes the item.

optionExplanations: 成本方向容易误导；这张卡关心的是大对象压垮数据库 I/O 和传输路径，而不是便宜存不存。
只有多写同一状态才会先看事务冲突；附件上传主要是大字节对象和网络搬运，不是抢同一行。
对：数据库适合索引小元数据，不适合反复写读大媒体；Chat Server 也不该变成文件中转站。
TTL 可以用在数据库行或对象存储对象上；它解决清理周期，不解决主路径里谁扛媒体流量。
optionExplanations_en: Cost would matter in an archive-cost discussion; this card is about database I/O and the upload path, not cheap storage.
Transaction contention matters when writers fight over the same state; attachment uploads are mainly large bytes and network transfer.
Right: keep metadata in the database, put media bytes in object storage, and keep Chat Server out of the file path.
TTL can expire rows or objects; cleanup does not fix which service has to carry the media bytes.

scenario: 媒体已改存 blob 存储并设 30 天 TTL，但上传字节仍先经过 Chat Server，带宽是这层的瓶颈。
scenario_en: Media now lands in blob storage with a thirty-day TTL, but the bytes still flow through the Chat Server, whose bandwidth is the bottleneck.
q: 「Chat Server 收下媒体再转存 blob 存储（30 天 TTL）」这个 Good 方案的遗留问题是？
q_en: What problem is left unsolved by the "Good" design where the Chat Server accepts media and forwards it to blob storage with a thirty-day TTL?
options: blob 存储比数据库更贵，这个成本方向的判断本身就说反了
Chat Server 仍要转发媒体，浪费一跳
无法生成预签名 URL
下载必须回源数据库
options_en: Claims blob storage is more expensive than a database — this gets the cost direction backwards
The Chat Server still has to forward every upload, a wasted hop
Pre-signed URLs cannot be generated this way
Downloads must still go back to the database
why: 转存方案解决了「别存数据库」，但媒体流量仍穿过 Chat Server；这一跳是纯浪费，于是引出预签名 URL 直传的 Great 方案。
why_en: The chat server still has to receive and forward every upload, a wasted hop that motivates letting clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为大二进制对象（图片、视频、附件）设计的存储服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage is an object store purpose-built for large binary files such as images, video, and attachments.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带临时签名和有效期的 URL，持有者不用额外身份验证就能直接读写对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL carries a temporary signature and expiry that lets whoever holds it read or write an object store directly without further authentication.

optionExplanations: blob 存储通常比数据库更便宜，成本方向说反了。
对：媒体流量仍然要先流经 Chat Server 再转存，这一跳纯粹是浪费。
预签名 URL 恰恰是可以生成的，正是后面 Great 方案要用的机制。
下载本可以直接从 blob 存储走，不必回源数据库，这不是这个方案的遗留问题。
optionExplanations_en: Blob storage is usually cheaper than a database, so this gets the cost direction backwards.
Right: media bytes still have to flow through Chat Server before landing in blob storage — that hop is pure waste.
Presigned URLs can absolutely be generated here — that's exactly the mechanism the next, better solution uses.
Downloads can go straight to blob storage without hitting the database, so that was never this design's leftover problem.

scenario: WhatsApp 类聊天要支持图片/视频附件。Chat Server 应负责鉴权和保存附件元数据，但大文件字节流不应该经过 Chat Server。
scenario_en: A WhatsApp-like chat system needs image and video attachments. The Chat Server should authorize access and store attachment metadata, but large media bytes should not flow through the Chat Server.
q: 理想的附件方案是？
q_en: What is the ideal design for attachments here?
options: 客户端直传到公开可写的存储桶，谁都能上传下载
把媒体 base64 编码后走 WebSocket 消息，拖慢聊天连接
上传走 FTP、下载走 HTTP，缺现代认证和加密
客户端换预签名 URL 直传 blob 存储，消息只带附件 URL
options_en: Have the client upload directly to a publicly writable bucket that anyone can read or write
Base64-encode the media and send it as a WebSocket message, which slows down the chat connection
Upload over FTP and download over HTTP, lacking modern authentication and encryption
The client exchanges for a presigned URL and uploads straight to blob storage; the message only carries the attachment URL
why: 这题要把控制面和数据面分开：Chat Server 管权限和元数据，Blob 存储承接真实文件字节。预签名 URL 让客户端直连对象存储，但权限仍由 Chat Server 先判断。
why_en: Separate the control plane from the data plane: the Chat Server handles authorization and metadata, while blob storage carries the actual media bytes. A pre-signed URL lets the client talk directly to object storage after the server authorizes it.
whenOtherWins: 若上传路径需要服务端处理（转码、病毒扫描、内容审核），让媒体先经过服务器反而有价值。
tradeoff: 客户端直传省 Chat Server 带宽 vs 经服务器中转换取服务端处理能力
diagram:
flowchart TD
    subgraph U["上传阶段：发送者"]
      S["发送客户端"] -->|"1 请求上传附件"| CS["Chat Server"]
      CS -->|"2 鉴权后返回 signed PUT URL"| S
      S -->|"3 文件 bytes 直传"| B[("Blob/Object 存储")]
      S -->|"4 sendMessage 只带 mediaId/objectKey"| CS
      CS -->|"5 保存消息和附件元数据"| DB[("Message DB")]
    end
    subgraph D["下载阶段：接收者"]
      R["接收客户端"] -->|"6 收到 mediaId 后请求下载权限"| CS
      CS -->|"7 返回 signed GET URL"| R
      R -->|"8 文件 bytes 直连下载"| B
    end
codeSample:
# small file: one signed PUT URL
PUT /bucket/att/9f2

# large file: signed URLs per part, then complete multipart upload
PUT /bucket/att/9f2?partNumber=1&uploadId=...
PUT /bucket/att/9f2?partNumber=2&uploadId=...
POST /bucket/att/9f2?uploadId=... # complete

termDefinitions.meaning: 带临时签名和有效期的 URL，持有者不用额外身份验证就能直接读写对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL carries a temporary signature and expiry that lets whoever holds it read or write an object store directly without further authentication.

termDefinitions.meaning: Binary Large Object 存储：按 objectKey 存图片、视频、附件这类不透明字节对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage stores opaque byte objects such as images, videos, and attachments, addressed by an object key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大文件直传方式：客户端把同一个 blob 拆成多个 part 直传到对象存储，最后由存储服务合成一个对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multipart upload lets the client upload one large object as multiple parts directly to object storage, then complete them into one object.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: 较老的文件传输协议，缺少现代认证和流式能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FTP is an older file-transfer protocol that lacks modern authentication and streaming support.

optionExplanations: 公开可写的桶谁都能上传下载，完全没有鉴权，安全上直接不可用。
base64 把二进制塞进消息体走 WebSocket，编码本身还会放大体积、拖慢连接。
FTP/HTTP 组合缺现代认证与加密，达不到本题隐含的安全要求。
对：Chat Server 先鉴权发预签名 URL，客户端凭它直传/直取 blob 存储，字节不经过服务器。
optionExplanations_en: A publicly writable bucket has no authorization at all — anyone can upload or download, unusable for security.
Base64-encoding binary into a WebSocket message body inflates size and slows down the connection.
An FTP-upload/HTTP-download combo lacks modern auth and encryption, falling short of this problem's implicit security bar.
Right: Chat Server authorizes first and issues a presigned URL; the client uses it to talk directly to blob storage, and bytes never touch the server.

scenario: WhatsApp 附件只在一个 ≤100 人的会话里分发，每份媒体最多被 100 个客户端各拉一次。
scenario_en: A WhatsApp attachment is only shared inside a chat of at most a hundred people, so each file is pulled about a hundred times.
q: 为什么这里给 blob 存储前面加 CDN 的收益有限？
q_en: Why is the payoff of putting a CDN in front of blob storage limited here?
options: CDN 无法传输图片视频
每个附件最多被 100 人下载，缓存复用率太低
CDN 与 TTL 冲突
预签名 URL 不能配 CDN，这个说法本身没有依据
options_en: A CDN cannot transfer images or video
Each attachment is downloaded by at most a hundred people, so cache reuse is too low
A CDN conflicts with TTL expiration
Claims a presigned URL can't be paired with a CDN — an unfounded restriction
why: CDN 的价值在「同一内容被海量用户重复拉取」；附件受众被 100 人上限封顶，命中复用少，加 CDN 属于低性价比。
why_en: Since at most one hundred participants will ever fetch an attachment, cache reuse is tiny and a CDN adds little value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点、就近返回的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers near users so it can be served locally.

termDefinitions.meaning: 带临时签名和有效期的 URL，持有者不用额外身份验证就能直接读写对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL carries a temporary signature and expiry that lets whoever holds it read or write an object store directly without further authentication.

optionExplanations: CDN 完全能传图片视频，问题不在文件类型本身。
对：每个附件最多被 100 人下载，命中复用率太低，CDN 缓存价值有限。
TTL 是存储层的过期策略，跟要不要加 CDN 边缘缓存没有冲突。
预签名 URL 完全可以配 CDN，两者不是互斥关系。
optionExplanations_en: A CDN can absolutely transfer images and video; the file type was never the issue.
Right: each attachment is downloaded by at most 100 people, so cache-hit reuse is too low for a CDN to pay off.
TTL is a storage-layer expiry policy and doesn't conflict with adding edge caching.
Presigned URLs can be paired with a CDN just fine; the two aren't mutually exclusive.

scenario: 在 WhatsApp 附件设计里，Chat Server 先鉴权，然后返回一个短期有效的预签名 URL。客户端拿这个 URL 直接把图片/视频上传到 blob 存储，下载时也从 blob 存储取，媒体字节不再经过 Chat Server。
scenario_en: In the WhatsApp attachment design, the Chat Server authorizes the request and returns a short-lived pre-signed URL. The client uploads images and video straight to blob storage with that URL, and downloads come from blob storage too, so media bytes never pass through the Chat Server.
q: 采用预签名 URL 直传附件后，哪些问题仍然没有自动解决？（多选）
q_en: After switching to direct pre-signed-URL uploads, which problems are still not automatically solved? (select all)
options: 如果想「所有接收者都下载完成后立刻删除附件」，还需要额外记录每个接收者的下载状态并触发删除
端到端加密、密钥分发、链接泄露后的访问控制等安全问题仍要额外设计
附件大小被限制在 1 MB 以内
媒体文件的上传字节流仍必须经过 Chat Server
options_en: If you want to delete the attachment immediately after every recipient downloads it, you still need per-recipient download tracking and a delete trigger
End-to-end encryption, key distribution, and access control after link leakage still need separate design
Attachment size is capped at 1 MB
The uploaded media bytes still have to pass through the Chat Server
why: 预签名 URL 只解决带宽和临时授权直连，不会自动追踪下载状态，也不会替你做端到端加密、密钥管理和权限收回。
why_en: A pre-signed URL only solves bandwidth and temporary authorization; it does not track downloads or handle encryption, key management, or revocation for you.
whenOtherWins: 如果附件必须先做服务端扫描、转码或合规审核，可以让上传先进入隔离区，再异步放行给接收者。
tradeoff: 预签名 URL 直传省带宽 vs 仍需独立设计生命周期和安全控制
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C[客户端] -->|请求上传权限| CS[Chat Server]
    CS -->|返回短期预签名 URL| C
    C -->|媒体字节直传| B[(Blob 存储)]
    B -->|TTL 到期自动删| X[默认过期]
    D[下载状态跟踪] -.额外设计.-> B
    K[加密和密钥管理] -.额外设计.-> C

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器用自己的存储凭证签出来的短期链接，客户端凭它直接上传或下载某个对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL is a short-lived link signed by the server with its storage credentials, letting the client upload or download one object directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储条目设置的存活期限，到期后由存储层自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TTL is an expiration time after which the storage layer automatically deletes the item.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有发送方和接收方能解密内容，服务器即使转发或存储也看不到明文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: End-to-end encryption means only the sender and recipients can decrypt the content; servers that relay or store it cannot read the plaintext.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专为图片、视频、附件等大二进制对象设计的对象存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage is object storage designed for large binary objects such as images, videos, and attachments.

optionExplanations: 预签名 URL 只解决直连授权，不会自动记录谁下载完了、要不要触发删除。
直传只省带宽和临时鉴权，端到端加密、密钥分发、泄露后收权都要另行设计。
附件大小上限不是预签名 URL 直传方案本身自动带来的限制，属于另设的产品规则。
预签名 URL 直传恰恰就是要把上传字节流从 Chat Server 移开，这个问题已经被解决了。
optionExplanations_en: A presigned URL only solves direct-connect authorization; it never tracks who finished downloading or triggers deletion on its own.
Direct upload only saves bandwidth and gives temporary auth — end-to-end encryption, key distribution, and revocation still need separate design.
An attachment size cap isn't something the presigned-URL pattern imposes automatically; that's a separate product rule.
Presigned direct upload is precisely what moves the upload byte stream off Chat Server, so this problem is already solved by it.

scenario: WhatsApp 级聊天应用有 10 亿注册用户。做容量估算时，先用「注册用户 × 同时在线比例」得到并发连接基数。
scenario_en: A WhatsApp-scale chat app has one billion registered users. Capacity estimation starts with registered users times the concurrent-online ratio to get the base connection count.
q: 按 20% 同时在线比例估算，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Estimating with a twenty-percent concurrent-online ratio, which conclusion does this most directly support?
options: 约 2000 万；服务器数量会被估小
约 10 亿；几乎所有注册用户都在线
约 2 亿；后续容量估算都以它为基数
无需估算；单机容量大就不看集群
options_en: About twenty million; server count would be underestimated
About one billion; almost every registered user is online
About two hundred million; later capacity estimates use it as the base
No estimate is needed if one host has high connection capacity
why: 估算标准：注册用户 × 同时在线比例。聊天应用可用 20% 粗估：10 亿 × 0.2 = 2 亿并发连接，再用它算服务器数、心跳量和轮询量。
why_en: Use registered users times the concurrent-online ratio; for chat, a rough 20% gives 1B × 0.2 = 200M connected users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时在线比例：某一时刻在线连接数占注册用户总数的粗略比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The concurrent-online ratio is the rough fraction of registered users connected at one moment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并发连接：同一时刻服务器需要同时维持的客户端连接数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concurrent connections are the client connections the servers must keep open at the same time.

scenario: WhatsApp 以单机（Erlang）可以撑住 100-200 万条 WebSocket 连接闻名，而同时在线连接数约 2 亿。
scenario_en: WhatsApp is famous for a single Erlang host holding one to two million WebSocket connections, while total concurrent connections are around two hundred million.
q: 把单机连接容量和总并发数放在一起看，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Putting per-host connection capacity next to total concurrency, which conclusion does that most directly support?
options: 单机容量被低估到 1-2 万，必须部署上万台服务器才够
单机能扛百万连接，但 2 亿并发仍需上百台服务器
单机连接容量足够大，2 亿并发只需要个位数台服务器
连接容量与服务器台数无关，只由带宽决定
options_en: Per-host capacity is underestimated at ten to twenty thousand, requiring tens of thousands of servers
Even at millions of connections per host, two hundred million concurrent users still needs hundreds of servers
Per-host capacity is large enough that a single-digit number of servers covers two hundred million users
Connection capacity has nothing to do with server count and is purely a function of bandwidth
why: WhatsApp 以单机 100-200 万连接闻名，但 2 亿并发还是要数百台服务器——「单机放不下」正是所有路由深挖的起点。
why_en: WhatsApp famously served one to two million connections per host, yet two hundred million concurrent users still demand hundreds of chat servers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为高并发、高容错设计的函数式编程语言，WhatsApp 早期靠它实现单机百万级连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Erlang is a functional programming language built for high concurrency and fault tolerance, which is how WhatsApp originally handled millions of connections per host.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

optionExplanations: 单机上限被压得太低，脱离了 WhatsApp 单机百万级连接这条已知事实。
对：服务器数 ≈ 总并发 / 单机容量，2 亿 / 百万级 ≈ 上百台，单机放不下才是扩展的起点。
个位数台服务器意味着单机容量被算成千万级，脱离了 100-200 万这条参考量级。
连接容量本质是内存/文件描述符/调度能力的函数，带宽只是其中一个约束，不是唯一变量。
optionExplanations_en: This underestimates single-machine capacity far below the known WhatsApp figure of roughly a million connections per box.
Right: server count ≈ total concurrency / per-machine capacity — 200M / ~1-2M is on the order of a hundred machines, which is exactly why routing needs to scale.
A single-digit server count implies per-machine capacity in the tens of millions, way beyond the 1-2M reference figure.
Connection capacity is mainly a function of memory, file descriptors, and scheduling — bandwidth is one constraint among several, not the only variable.

scenario: WhatsApp 的在线连接超出单机上限，你在 L4 负载均衡器后面直接加了几十台 Chat Server。
scenario_en: WhatsApp outgrows a single box, so you add dozens of Chat Servers behind an L4 load balancer.
q: 「只往 L4 LB 后面加更多 Chat Server」这个天真方案为什么直接失败？
q_en: Why does the naive plan of just adding more Chat Servers behind an L4 load balancer fail outright?
options: LB 撑不住 WebSocket 握手
服务器未必持有接收者的连接，无法投递
服务器数量太多成本失控
DynamoDB 不支持多个写入者
options_en: The load balancer can't handle WebSocket handshakes
The server has no guarantee of holding the recipients' connections, so it cannot deliver
Too many servers make the cost spiral out of control
DynamoDB does not support multiple writers
why: 连接只活在某台服务器的内存里；水平扩容后发送方和接收方大概率不在同一台，裸加机器根本无法投递。面试里千万别停在这一步。
why_en: A server that accepts a message has no guarantee of holding the recipients' connections, so naive horizontal scaling simply cannot deliver events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

optionExplanations: LB 转发连接本身没问题，握手不是这个方案失败的原因。
对：接住消息的那一端未必是接住连接的那一端，裸加机器解决不了「找不到人在哪」这件事。
成本确实会涨，但这不是「直接失败」的根因，根因是投递不到人。
DynamoDB 支持多个写入者，这里的失败跟数据库写入者数量无关。
optionExplanations_en: Forwarding connections through an LB isn't the issue here — handshakes aren't why this fails.
Right: a connection only lives in one server's memory, so after scaling out, sender and recipient are usually on different machines and delivery just fails.
Cost does go up, but that's not why it fails outright — the real cause is delivery has nowhere to land.
DynamoDB supports multiple writers just fine; the failure here has nothing to do with database writer counts.

scenario: 裸加 Chat Server 无法投递之后，一个常见的直觉方案是借助消息队列：为系统里的每个用户单独建一条队列 topic 当它的收件箱。
scenario_en: Once naively adding Chat Servers fails to deliver messages, a common instinct is to reach for a message queue: give every user in the system their own topic to act as their inbox.
q: 「每个用户一个 Kafka topic 当 Inbox」为什么行不通？
q_en: Why doesn't giving every user their own Kafka topic as an inbox work?
options: Kafka 不支持多消费者订阅
Kafka 无法持久化消息
topic 无法动态创建，这也不是这里的真正瓶颈
Kafka 不是为数十亿 topic 设计的，元数据开销太大
options_en: Kafka does not support multiple consumers on one topic
Kafka cannot persist messages
Topics cannot be created dynamically, but that is not the real bottleneck either
Kafka is not built for billions of topics; the metadata overhead is too large
why: 每用户一个 Kafka topic 太重：元数据随 topic 数线性增长。Kafka 也不擅长按 clientId+messageId 精确查 pending 并删除，Message+Inbox 表更适合。
why_en: A Kafka topic per user is too heavy and awkward for per-client ACK and delete, while a Message plus Inbox table can query and clear pending rows by clientId and messageId.
whenOtherWins: Kafka 仍然适合做少量 shared topics 的后台事件流，例如消息审计、异步通知任务、反垃圾处理或分析流水线；它不适合把 topic 粒度做到每个终端用户。
tradeoff: Kafka 顺序日志的高吞吐 vs Inbox 表按 client/message 精确查询和清理
