termDefinitions.meaning: 把消息持久化到磁盘、按 topic/partition 组织、并维护消费者位点的分布式日志/消息系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log and messaging system that persists messages to disk, organizes them into topics and partitions, and tracks consumer offsets.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 里的一条命名日志流，通常还会拆成多个 partition；它不是轻量到可以为每个用户随便创建的 row。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Kafka topic is a named log stream, usually split into partitions; it is not a lightweight row that you can create once per user at massive scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis Pub/Sub 里的频道名，通常不需要提前创建；只有订阅关系、连接和输出缓冲区等内存状态，不保存消息历史或 consumer offset。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis Pub/Sub channel is a channel name that usually does not need to be pre-created; Redis mainly keeps in-memory subscription mappings, connections, and output buffers, not message history or consumer offsets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者在某个 Kafka partition 上已经读到哪里的位置。它适合顺序消费，不等于 Inbox 表里每条 message 的独立 ack 状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer offset records how far a consumer has read in a Kafka partition. It fits ordered consumption, but it is not the same as independent ACK state for each message in an Inbox table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 chatId 保存会话内消息历史和顺序的日志。它回答“这个会话发生了什么”，不是直接回答“这台设备还缺什么”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chat log stores message history and ordering by chatId. It answers what happened in this conversation, not directly what this device is still missing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一个 chat 的消息放到同一分区/同一有序流，适合保证会话内顺序；但离线补发还需要 per-client 的 ack 或 Inbox 状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Partitioning by chatId puts messages from the same chat into one partition or ordered stream, which is good for conversation ordering; offline redelivery still needs per-client ACK or Inbox state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 user/client 存 pending messageId 的表；重连时按 key 查，ack 后精确删除或标记某条待投递记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Inbox table stores pending message ids by user or client; reconnect queries by key, and ACK precisely deletes or marks one pending delivery row.

optionExplanations: Kafka 天生支持多消费者订阅同一 topic，这不是它在这里的短板。
Kafka 恰恰擅长持久化，问题不在能不能存住消息。
topic 确实可以动态创建，这不是真正卡住它的地方。
对：数十亿用户对应数十亿 topic，controller 元数据和 partition 开销会失控，Kafka 不是为这个粒度设计的。
optionExplanations_en: Kafka natively supports multiple consumers subscribing to one topic, so that isn't the weakness here.
Kafka is actually good at persistence, so durability was never the problem.
Topics can be created dynamically just fine, so that isn't the real blocker either.
Right: billions of users would mean billions of topics, and controller metadata plus partition overhead spirals out of control — Kafka isn't built for that granularity.

scenario: 想让「谁负责哪个用户」变成确定映射：按 userId 一致性哈希把用户固定分配到 Chat Server，服务器之间直连投递。
scenario_en: You want "which server owns which user" to be a deterministic mapping: consistent-hash users by userId onto a fixed Chat Server, and deliver via direct server-to-server connections.
q: 这个方案还需要什么配套基础设施？
q_en: What supporting infrastructure does this approach still require?
options: 中心注册表（ZooKeeper/etcd）记录哈希段归属
一个全局关系型数据库存路由状态，高频写入很快成为瓶颈点
客户端向全网广播自己的位置
DNS 泛解析到任意服务器
options_en: A central registry (ZooKeeper/etcd) records which hash range each server owns
A single global relational database stores routing state, and high-frequency writes quickly become the bottleneck
Clients broadcast their own location to the entire network
Wildcard DNS resolves to an arbitrary server
why: 一致性哈希直连需要强一致控制面：server 列表、hash range owner、ring version、租约和故障接管。ZooKeeper/etcd 适合这类 watch/lease；Redis 当事实源就要自补选主和脑裂保护。
why_en: Consistent-hash direct routing needs a strongly consistent control plane for membership, range ownership, ring versions, leases, and failover, which fits ZooKeeper or etcd better than Redis.
whenOtherWins: 不想自己管理伸缩编排、能接受多一跳毫秒级延迟时，Redis Pub/Sub 更省心，也是文中评级更高的选择。
tradeoff: 服务器直连低时延 vs 自管路由编排（注册表、扩容迁移）的运维复杂度
diagram:
flowchart LR ZK["ZooKeeper/etcd
ring version + hash ranges"] --> CS1["Chat Server A
owns range 0-30"] ZK --> CS2["Chat Server B
owns range 31-60"] ZK --> CS3["Chat Server C
owns range 61-99"] Client["Client userId"] --> LB["L4 Load Balancer"] LB --> Gateway["Gateway/Chat Server
compute hash(userId)"] Gateway --> CS2 CS2 --> Peer["Direct server-to-server delivery"] CS3 -. "lease expires" .-> ZK ZK --> Reassign["Publish new ring version"] Reassign --> CS1 Reassign --> CS2
codeSample:
# Control plane: server registration and hash-ring ownership
onServerStart(serverId, address):
  zk.createEphemeral(f"/chat/servers/{serverId}", address)
  ring = zk.get("/chat/hash-ring")
  ownedRanges = ring.rangesFor(serverId)
  openPeerConnections(ring.servers)

# Routing: deterministic owner lookup from a strongly consistent ring version
routeToOwner(userId, msg):
  ring = localRingCache.current()
  owner = ring.ownerOf(hash(userId))
  sendDirect(owner.address, msg)

# Scaling: coordinator publishes a new ring version
rebalance(newServers):
  newRing = computeRing(newServers)
  zk.compareAndSet("/chat/hash-ring", expectedVersion, newRing)
  # watchers notify chat servers; they drain/migrate affected users

高频路由查写通常太重

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式协调服务，常用来做服务注册、leader 选举、配置发布、临时节点和 watch 通知。适合保存“谁负责哪段 hash range”这种控制面事实源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a distributed coordination service used for service registration, leader election, configuration publishing, ephemeral nodes, and watch notifications. It is a good source of truth for control-plane metadata such as which server owns which hash range.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式强一致键值存储，常用于服务发现和配置管理；Kubernetes 也用它保存集群状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a strongly consistent distributed key-value store commonly used for service discovery and configuration; Kubernetes also uses it to store cluster state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 key 和节点都映射到同一个哈希环上，节点增减时只影响环上相邻的一小段映射关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing places both keys and nodes on the same hash ring so adding or removing a node only reshuffles a small neighboring slice of the mapping.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责配置、服务发现、成员关系、路由规则等“系统怎么运行”的元数据路径；更新较少，但一致性要求高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The control plane manages metadata about how the system runs, such as configuration, service discovery, membership, and routing rules; it changes less often but needs strong consistency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责真正承载用户请求和消息转发的高频路径，例如 Redis Pub/Sub 转发消息、Chat Server 写 WebSocket。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The data plane carries high-frequency user traffic and message forwarding, such as Redis Pub/Sub relaying messages or Chat Servers writing to WebSockets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 租约或临时节点表示“只要这个服务器还活着，这条注册记录就存在”；服务器宕机或会话断开后记录自动失效，其他节点能及时接管。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lease or ephemeral node means the registration exists only while the server is alive; if the server crashes or its session expires, the record disappears and others can take over.

termDefinitions.meaning: 高性能内存数据结构服务，适合缓存、计数器、presence、Pub/Sub 等高频数据面任务；也能存配置，但不如 ZooKeeper/etcd 专门面向集群协调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is a high-performance in-memory data-structure service suited for caching, counters, presence, and Pub/Sub data-plane tasks. It can store configuration, but it is not as specialized for cluster coordination as ZooKeeper or etcd.

optionExplanations: 对：这类强一致协调组件天生支持 watch 和租约，正好覆盖归属变更和故障接管。
关系型数据库能持久化，但高频路由查写和集群协调对它来说通常太重，容易反成瓶颈。
客户端广播位置既没有一致性保证，也没有故障检测，扩容一次就可能全网状态不一致。
DNS 泛解析不带路由状态，无法回答「这个 userId 现在归哪台服务器」这个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Right: ZooKeeper/etcd offer watches, leases, and strongly consistent writes — exactly the coordination semantics needed to track hash-range ownership and failover.
A relational database can persist state, but high-frequency routing reads/writes and cluster coordination are usually too heavy for it and can become the bottleneck.
Clients broadcasting their own location has no consistency guarantee or failure detection — one rescale and the network-wide state can drift out of sync.
Wildcard DNS carries no routing state, so it can't answer "which server currently owns this userId."

q: 一致性哈希直连方案要付出哪些代价？（多选）
q_en: What costs does the consistent-hashing direct-connect approach pay? (select all)
options: 每台 Chat Server 都要与所有其他 Chat Server 保持连接，迫使服务器「个头大、数量少」
扩容 / 缩容要精细编排连接迁移，避免用户集体重连引发惊群
伸缩过渡期要向新旧两台服务器同时发送事件，防止丢消息
userId 从此不能再作数据库分区键
options_en: Every Chat Server must stay connected to every other Chat Server, forcing servers to be few and large
Scaling in or out requires carefully orchestrated connection draining to avoid a thundering herd
During a scaling transition, events must be sent to both the old and new owning server so nothing is lost
userId can no longer be used as a database partition key
why: 一致性哈希让「谁管哪个用户」人人可算，直连投递省掉 Redis 那一跳；代价是全网状连接近 N²、扩缩容换主要防惊群、迁移窗口要双发。
why_en: Consistent hashing makes ownership of each user something every server can compute, and direct delivery skips the Redis hop. You pay for it with a near-N-squared mesh, a reconnect thundering herd whenever ownership shifts, and dual-sending during migration.
tradeoff: 直连低延迟、少一跳 vs 自己维护全网连接、哈希环迁移和过渡期双发
codeSample:
# Before scaling:
owner(user123) = Server A

# Add Server B; hash ring changes:
oldOwner = Server A
newOwner = Server B

# Transition window:
route(user123) -> [oldOwner, newOwner]  # dual-send or bridge
oldOwner.drainConnections(batch_size=small)
client reconnects with jitter/backoff

# After client is stable on B:
route(user123) -> Server B only

termDefinitions.meaning: 大量客户端因同一事件在同一时刻集体重连或重试，瞬间打垮后端的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thundering herd happens when a huge number of clients reconnect or retry at the same instant and overwhelm the backend.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一行数据被分配到哪个物理分区的键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which physical partition a row of data lands on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每台 Chat Server 都和其他 Chat Server 建连接。服务器数 N 增长时，连接关系接近 N²，数量越多越难维护。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full mesh means every Chat Server connects to every other Chat Server. As the number of servers N grows, connection relationships approach N squared and become harder to maintain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缩容或迁移时不再接新连接，并把已有连接分批迁走，避免用户同时重连。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Connection draining means a server stops accepting new connections and gradually moves existing connections away during scale-in or migration to avoid simultaneous reconnects.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希变更前负责某个 userId 的服务器叫 old owner，变更后负责它的服务器叫 new owner。迁移窗口里两者要协调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The old owner is the server responsible for a userId before a consistent-hash change, and the new owner is responsible after the change. They must coordinate during the migration window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把服务器和 key(这里 userId)都哈希到一个环上，key 归顺时针方向第一台服务器管。相比 hash(key)%N「加减一台就几乎全体重映射」，它加减一台只挪约 1/N 的 key，极大减少伸缩时的数据/连接迁移。常配「虚拟节点」(每台在环上多个点)让分布更均匀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing places both servers and keys (here userId) on a ring; a key is owned by the first server clockwise. Versus hash(key)%N, which remaps almost every key when N changes, it moves only ~1/N of keys when a server is added/removed, greatly cutting reshuffle on scaling. Virtual nodes (many ring points per server) even out distribution.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每台服务器用共享的哈希环自己算出目标用户归哪台管，直接开连接把消息递过去，不经 Redis 等中间件。好处是省一跳、延迟低;代价是全网状互连(≈N²)+ 自己管路由控制面(环、归属、故障接管、连接迁移)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direct delivery: each server uses the shared hash ring to compute which server owns the target user and connects directly to hand off the message, with no Redis in between. Pro: one fewer hop, lower latency; con: full-mesh interconnect (≈N²) plus self-managing the routing control plane (ring, ownership, failover, connection migration).

optionExplanations: 全网状互连意味着服务器要「个头大、数量少」才压得住 N² 连接数，这是选它必须接受的代价。
扩容/缩容换 owner 时，若不精细编排迁移，大量用户会同时重连造成惊群。
迁移窗口内旧值和新值都可能是当前归属，不双发或桥接就会有事件打空。
userId 依然可以作数据库分区键，路由哈希和存储分区是两套独立机制，互不冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Full mesh connectivity means servers must be "big and few" to keep N² connections manageable — that's a cost you accept by choosing this approach.
When scale-out/in reassigns owners, users can reconnect en masse and cause a thundering herd unless migration is carefully orchestrated.
During the migration window either the old or new value can be the current owner, so without dual-write or bridging some events land on nobody.
userId can still serve as the database partition key — routing hashing and storage partitioning are two independent mechanisms that don't conflict.
scenario: 用一致性哈希把 userId 确定映射到某台 Chat Server，服务器之间直连投递(不经 Redis)。
scenario_en: Use consistent hashing to deterministically map userId to a Chat Server; servers deliver by connecting directly (no Redis).

scenario: 上百台 Chat Server 之间要互相转发消息，接收者可能连在任何一台上；希望用现成的轻量组件专门做服务器间的消息中转。
scenario_en: Hundreds of Chat Servers need to forward messages to each other since a recipient could be connected to any of them; you want an off-the-shelf lightweight component dedicated to that inter-server relay.
q: 文中评为最优（Great）的方案是？
q_en: Which approach does the article rate as the best ("Great") solution?
options: RabbitMQ 配死信队列
每用户一个 Kafka topic
Redis Pub/Sub：按 userId 建频道服务器间转发
Chat Server 之间用 gRPC 全网状广播，人人互连开销随规模平方增长
options_en: RabbitMQ with a dead-letter queue
A Kafka topic per user
Redis Pub/Sub: a channel per userId for server-to-server relay

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线迁移路由方案(旧→新)时有个窗口:你不知道某接收者此刻在听旧路还是新路(如服务器还没订上新群频道)。于是窗口内两边都发，谁都不漏(防丢)，等确认新路完全就绪再停老路。重复用 messageId 去重——宁可临时重复(可去重)也不丢消息(at-least-once + dedup)。卡040 的「旧主/新主双发」是同一个模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dual-send during migration: when switching a routing scheme live (old→new) there is a window where you do not know whether a given receiver is listening on the old or new path (e.g. a server has not yet subscribed to the new group channel). So you send on both during the window so nobody is missed (loss prevention), stopping the old path only once the new one is confirmed ready. Duplicates are removed by messageId — prefer temporary (dedupable) duplicates over loss (at-least-once + dedup). Card 040's old/new-owner dual-send is the same pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向连接、保证有序送达的传输层协议。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP keepalive is a low-frequency operating-system TCP probe for idle connections. It checks whether the connection is still alive, but it has no chat-specific semantics and is often slow by default.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器还以为 socket 活着，但客户端或网络路径已经不可用。继续向它写消息可能超时或静默失败。

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层定时 ping/pong，小包里还可以带最新 sequence number，用来确认连接还活着并发现客户端是否落后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is an application-level periodic ping/pong; it can also carry the latest sequence number to confirm the connection is alive and detect whether the client is behind.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由聊天服务自己定义的协议逻辑，比如 WebSocket ping/pong、消息 ack 超时、重连后 sync；它比 TCP 层更懂业务目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An application-level mechanism is protocol logic defined by the chat service, such as WebSocket ping/pong, message ACK timeouts, and reconnect sync. It understands the product's latency and delivery goals better than the TCP layer.

应用层心跳可以自己设定间隔，通常比 TCP keepalive 更快而不是更慢。
optionExplanations_en: Right: TCP keepalive relies on occasional kernel-level probes, often minutes apart; an application-level heartbeat can probe on a timer, down to seconds.
The two differ by an order of magnitude, not "comparable" — that gap is exactly why an app-level mechanism gets added.
TCP keepalive isn't millisecond-scale; its probe interval is typically minutes, much slower than an app-level heartbeat.
An app-level heartbeat can set its own interval and is typically faster than TCP keepalive, not slower.

Blindly send every message twice, masking loss with redundancy

q_en: Fill in the formula for the heartbeat detection upper bound:
text: 心跳间隔 {{10}} 秒、pong 超时 {{5}} 秒时，任何死连接最迟 {{15}} 秒内被发现——心跳给出的是检测时间的保证上界。
why: 上界 = 间隔 + 超时(最坏是刚回完 pong 就死，要等近一个间隔才发下次 ping，再等满超时)。间隔换检测速度↔ping 流量，超时换抗抖动↔检测延迟。
why_en: The upper bound is interval plus timeout: worst case the connection dies right after a pong, so you wait nearly a full interval before the next ping and then the full timeout. Interval trades detection speed against ping traffic; timeout trades jitter tolerance against detection delay.

scenario: Pub/Sub 尽力而为可能漏推，需要给已连接客户端一个最朴素的兜底手段拿回漏掉的消息。
scenario_en: Pub/Sub's best-effort delivery can drop a push; connected clients need the simplest possible backstop for recovering a missed message.
q: 这个兜底方案是？
q_en: What is that backstop mechanism?
options: 客户端重启即可
直接信任 Pub/Sub 绝不会丢消息，跳过兜底设计
客户端定时发 sync 请求，服务器补发未投递消息
每天凌晨做一次全量同步
options_en: Just have the client restart
Simply trusts Pub/Sub to never lose a message and skips a fallback altogether
Clients periodically send a sync request and the server pushes undelivered messages
Run one full sync for everyone at midnight
why: Pub/Sub 丢的是实时提醒，不是消息本体。发送路径先写 Message+Inbox 再推送；没 ack 的 Inbox row 留着，之后由 sync、重连、序号缺口或心跳补回来。
why_en: Pub/Sub can lose a realtime notification, but Message and Inbox remain durable until ACK, so sync, reconnect, sequence gaps, or heartbeats can recover it.
codeSample:
sendMessage(msg):
  db.put(Message[msg.id] = msg)
  db.put(Inbox[receiverId, msg.id] = PENDING)
  pubsub.publish(userChannel(receiverId), msg.id)  # best effort

sync(receiverId):
  pending = db.query(Inbox where receiverId and status = PENDING)
  sendOverWebSocket(pending)

ack(receiverId, msgId):
  db.delete(Inbox[receiverId, msgId])  # or mark DELIVERED

对：客户端记 lastSeq，收到更大的 seq 却跳号，缺口本身就是「漏消息」的证据，立刻请求同步。

The sequence number comes from an INCR at the sender side, a separate concern from load-balancing policy.
Right: the client tracks lastSeq, and a gap when a higher seq arrives is itself the evidence of a missed message, triggering an immediate resync.

codeSample:
# Send path: assign one global sequence per recipient user
sendMessage(toUserId, chatId, body):
  seq = redis.incr(f"seq:user:{toUserId}")
  msgId = newId()
  Message.put(chatId=chatId, msgId=msgId, userSeq=seq, body=body)
  for clientId in Clients.query(toUserId):
    Inbox.put(clientId=clientId, msgId=msgId, chatId=chatId, userSeq=seq, status="PENDING")
  redis.publish(f"user:{toUserId}", { "msgId": msgId, "seq": seq })

# Existing heartbeat: add latestSeq to the ping payload
sendHeartbeat(userId, ws):
  latestSeq = getLatestSeq(userId)  # Redis GET, local cache, or replicated presence state
  ws.send({ "type": "ping", "latestSeq": latestSeq })

# Client side: detect missed pushes without waiting for the next chat message
onMessage(msg):
  if msg.seq > local.lastSeq + 1:
    syncInbox(fromSeq=local.lastSeq + 1, toSeq=msg.seq - 1)
  apply(msg)
  local.lastSeq = max(local.lastSeq, msg.seq)
  ack(msg.msgId)

onHeartbeatPing(latestSeq):
  if latestSeq > local.lastSeq:
    syncInbox(fromSeq=local.lastSeq + 1, toSeq=latestSeq)
  sendPong({ "lastSeq": local.lastSeq })

syncInbox(fromSeq, toSeq):
  rows = Inbox.query(clientId=local.clientId, userSeqBetween=[fromSeq, toSeq])
  for row in rows:
    msg = Message.get(row.chatId, row.msgId)
    apply(msg)
    ack(row.msgId)

q: 用哪条 Redis 命令原子地生成下一个序号？
q_en: Which Redis command atomically generates the next sequence number?
options: GET seq:user:123 之后再 SET 加一
INCR seq:user:123
EXPIRE seq:user:123 60
PUBLISH seq:user:123 next
options_en: GET seq:user:123 and then SET it plus one
INCR seq:user:123
EXPIRE seq:user:123 60
PUBLISH seq:user:123 next
why: GET+SET 是两步读改写，并发下可能撞号；INCR 对单个 Redis key 原子自增并返回新值。它只保证单命令单 key，不等于多 key 事务，也不保证故障切换绝不回退。
why_en: GET plus SET can race, while INCR atomically increments one Redis key and returns a unique value; it is not a multi-key transaction or failover guarantee.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要会话内定序，可按 chat 计数（INCR seq:chat:456）；全局用户序号的优势是一个数字覆盖该用户所有会话的丢失检测。
tradeoff: INCR 单 key 原子自增 vs GET+SET 两步读改写的竞态风险

q: 生产系统实践中通常怎样组合可靠投递的三种机制？
q_en: How do production systems typically combine the three reliable-delivery mechanisms?
options: 只用轮询，简单可靠
认为只用心跳就能覆盖连接和消息两类故障
三者互补：心跳测连接，序号测漏消息，轮询兜底

why: 三种机制对应三类故障：连接死了靠心跳、消息漏了靠序号、以上都失灵还有轮询。关键盲区：序号只有「后面还有下一条」才暴露缺口，若最后一条丢了、又没有新消息，序号和心跳都发现不了——轮询定时主动问一遍 Inbox 兜住它。
why_en: Three mechanisms cover three failure modes: heartbeat for dead connections, sequence numbers for lost messages, polling as the last resort. Key blind spot: a sequence gap only shows when a later message arrives, so if the last message is lost and none follows, neither sequence nor heartbeat notices — periodic polling of the Inbox catches it.

Pull/polling = the client asks on a timer (simple, connection-agnostic, but adds latency and heavy request volume). For reliable delivery, push is primary and pull is the fallback.

q_en: What is the article's stance on out-of-order messages?

所有消息经单一队列串行化
统一延迟 5 秒再排序显示

Use vector clocks for total-order broadcast
Serialize every message through a single queue
Uniformly delay display by 5 seconds to let reordering happen

why_en: The design deliberately does not enforce strict ordering because chat users prefer seeing new messages fast over guaranteed order.

optionExplanations: 对：不做严格重排、直接按服务器时间戳展示，用户要的是「新消息尽快出现」，不是绝对全局顺序。

optionExplanations_en: Right: skip strict reordering and show by server-received timestamp — users want new messages fast, not a strict global order.
Vector clocks give causal ordering, but the implementation and reasoning cost far outweighs what a chat app needs.
Funneling every write through a single serial queue crushes concurrency, trading away throughput and latency for little gain.
Delaying everything by seconds to sort trades real-time delivery for strict ordering — the opposite of what "users want new messages fast" implies.

scenario: 所有 Chat Server 需要给消息一个统一、可复现的展示顺序，即使到达顺序不同。
scenario_en: Every Chat Server needs to give messages one consistent, reproducible display order, even when they arrive in a different order.
q: 补全消息排序的实际做法：
q_en: Fill in the actual approach to message ordering:
text: 所有 Chat Server 经 {{NTP}} 同步时钟；消息到达时盖上{{服务器接收}}时间戳，客户端一律按此时间戳排序展示，从而让所有客户端看到{{一致}}的顺序。
why: NTP 把各 Chat Server 的钟拉齐到几毫秒内，服务器接收时间才成为跨机可比的排序键，不信客户端时间。再用 (server_ts, server_id, message_id) 全序组合，各端排出同一顺序。
why_en: NTP pulls every Chat Server's clock to within a few milliseconds, which is what makes server-received time a sort key you can compare across hosts; client time is not trusted. Then a total tuple of server timestamp, server id, and message id makes every client render the same order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一堆机器的时钟通过网络对齐到同一参考时间的协议(源头是原子钟/GPS，经 stratum 分层下发，还会扣掉网络往返延迟)。作用:把各 Chat Server 的钟拉齐到几毫秒内，使「服务器接收时间」成为跨服务器可比的排序键。它够好但不完美——残留几 ms~几十 ms 偏差，所以排序偶有 pop-in。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP (Network Time Protocol) synchronizes machine clocks over a network to a common reference (rooted at atomic/GPS clocks, distributed through strata, accounting for round-trip delay). Here it aligns Chat Server clocks to within a few ms so "server-received time" is a cross-server-comparable sort key. Good-enough but imperfect — residual ms-to-tens-of-ms skew causes occasional pop-in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个「对任意两条消息都能分出先后、且在所有客户端上判定完全一致」的排序键。单用 server_ts 不够(可能相等)，要补确定性 tie-breaker：(server_ts, server_id, message_id)。这样相同时间戳也被所有端排出逐字节相同的顺序 = 可复现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A total-order sort key can order any two messages and does so identically on all clients. server_ts alone is insufficient (values can tie); add a deterministic tie-breaker: (server_ts, server_id, message_id). Then even equal timestamps sort byte-identically everywhere = reproducible.

    msg.server_ts = now()       # NTP 同步过的本机时钟；各 server 差几 ms 内
    msg.server_id = SERVER_ID   # 平局时的 tie-breaker
    persist(msg)                # 写 Message 表，server_ts 当排序键
    fan_out(msg)                # 推给各接收者（到达顺序不保证）

# —— 客户端：展示时一律按戳排序 ——
def render(inbox):
    # 关键：排序键要"全序且确定"，所有客户端才排出完全相同的顺序
    msgs = sorted(inbox.all(),
                  key=lambda m: (m.server_ts, m.server_id, m.message_id))
    display(msgs)               # 新消息可能插到已显示消息上方 = pop-in（卡074）

scenario: WhatsApp 按服务器接收时间排序消息，各 Chat Server 的钟靠 NTP 对齐到几毫秒内。
scenario_en: WhatsApp orders messages by server-received time, with Chat Server clocks aligned to within a few milliseconds by NTP.
q: 按服务器接收时间排序的可见副作用是什么？
q_en: What is the visible side effect of ordering messages by server-received time?
options: 部分消息会永久丢失
偶尔消息会插到发送更晚的消息上方，用户能接受
时钟漂移会让消息重复
认为客户端必须缓存全部历史消息才能排序
options_en: Some messages are permanently lost
Occasionally a message pops in above one sent later, and users find it acceptable
Clock drift causes duplicate messages
Claims the client must cache the entire message history just to sort it
why: 接收时间 ≠ 发送时间，偶发的 pop-in 在所难免；但这是拿微小的视觉瑕疵换实时性，用户买账。
why_en: Occasionally a message pops in above one that was actually sent later, and users find that acceptable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台服务器把时钟对齐到同一参考时间的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes server clocks to a shared reference time.

optionExplanations: 消息本体仍然完整保存并展示，不会因为排序键选择而永久丢失。
对：排序键换成了服务器视角而不是发送方视角，两者出现分歧时用户看到的顺序会跳一下，但能接受。
时钟漂移影响的是排序先后，不会凭空复制出重复消息。
按接收时间排序不需要客户端缓存全部历史，跟这个副作用无关。
optionExplanations_en: The message body is still fully stored and displayed — nothing is permanently lost by this choice of sort key.
Right: received time isn't send time, so an occasional pop-in (a later-sent message appearing above an earlier one) is unavoidable but acceptable to users.
Clock drift affects ordering, not message duplication — it doesn't spawn extra copies.
Sorting by received time doesn't require the client to cache full history; that isn't this side effect.

scenario: 20 亿 WhatsApp 用户每 10 秒回一次心跳，个人资料页还要显示 last seen 时间。
scenario_en: Two billion WhatsApp users answer a heartbeat every ten seconds, and the profile screen still has to show a last-seen time.
q: 「用户每次发消息 / 收消息 / 回心跳都更新一次 lastSeen 字段」这个 naive 方案的问题？
q_en: What is the problem with the naive design of updating a lastSeen field every time a user sends a message, receives a message, or answers a heartbeat?
options: 读取延迟太高，其实读一条记录很快
巨大写放大：心跳把写入推到百万级/秒，且数据立刻过时
时间戳精度不够，这不是这里的真正问题
会暴露用户隐私 IP，其实字段里没有 IP
options_en: Read latency becomes too high, but reading one record is actually fast
Massive write amplification: heartbeats push writes to millions per second, and the data is stale the instant it lands
Timestamp precision is insufficient, but that is not the real problem here
It leaks user IP addresses, but the field never stores an IP
why: 每个活动都写库，写入量被心跳放大到数百万/秒，换来的却是「查到时已过时」的数据——成本与价值完全倒挂。
why_en: Updating last seen on every action creates millions of low-value writes per second that are stale the moment they land, paying for consistency nobody needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测包，用来确认对方仍然存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small probe message sent at a fixed interval to confirm the other side of a connection is still alive.

optionExplanations: 读一条记录本身很快，读取延迟不是这个 naive 方案的问题所在。
对：把高频活动直接变成写库操作，量级会被心跳持续放大，而查到的值本来就该是近似值。
时间戳精度足够表达秒级的在线状态变化，精度不是这里的真正问题。
字段里只存时间戳，没有 IP 信息，不存在隐私暴露的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Reading a single row is fast; read latency was never this naive design's problem.
Right: heartbeats push write frequency into the millions per second, and what you get back is already stale by the time you read it — cost and value are completely inverted.
Timestamp precision is more than enough to express second-level online-state changes; precision isn't the real issue.
The field only stores a timestamp, no IP — there's no privacy exposure here.

scenario: 要做「最后在线时间」，希望存储与写入都最小化。两个洞察：用户断连时服务器一定知道；用户在线时他自己能实时告诉你。
scenario_en: You want to build "last seen" while minimizing both storage and writes. Two insights: the server always knows when a user disconnects, and an online user can tell you about it in real time.
q: 文中的设计是？
q_en: What is the article's design?
options: 只在断连时写一条记录，查询时并行读表并经 Pub/Sub 探活，合并显示
每分钟对全体在线用户做快照，负载随在线人数线性增长
客户端之间 P2P 互相询问，对方离线时完全查不到结果，也没权限校验
在负载均衡器上采集日志离线分析，只能查历史查不了当下
options_en: Write one row only on disconnect; on query, read it in parallel with a Pub/Sub probe and merge the results
Snapshot every online user once a minute; load grows linearly with the number of online users
Clients query each other peer-to-peer; when the other side is offline there's no result at all, and it skips permission checks too
Collect logs on the load balancer and analyze offline; can only answer historical queries, never the current state
why: 最小写入方案是断连时写 LastSeen，查询时并行读 LastSeen 并经 Pub/Sub 探活目标 Chat Server。在线就显示 online；没响应才回退 lastDisconnect。
why_en: Write LastSeen only on disconnect, then answer reads by combining that durable row with a live Pub/Sub presence probe; load-balancer logs are analytics, not the presence source of truth.
whenOtherWins: 用户量小或需要完整在线历史审计时，按活动直接写库更简单、信息也更全。
tradeoff: 存储与写入最小化 vs 在线状态的实时精确性
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Querying client
    participant API as Chat API
    participant LS as LastSeen table
    participant PS as Pub/Sub
    participant CS as Target Chat Server
    A->>API: getLastSeen(targetUserId)
    par historical fallback
      API->>LS: read lastDisconnect(targetUserId)
      LS-->>API: 10:32:05
    and live presence probe
      API->>PS: ask user:target are you online?
      PS->>CS: presence probe
      CS-->>API: online if connection exists
    end
    API-->>A: online OR last seen at 10:32:05
codeSample:
onDisconnect(userId):
  LastSeen.conditionalUpdate(
    key=userId,
    set={ "lastDisconnect": now() },
    condition="new timestamp is newer"
  )

getLastSeen(viewerId, targetUserId):
  historical = LastSeen.get(targetUserId)  # durable fallback
  live = pubsub.request(
    channel=f"user:{targetUserId}",
    message={ "type": "presenceProbe" },
    timeout_ms=150
  )

  if live == "ONLINE":
    return { "status": "online" }
  return { "status": "offline", "lastSeen": historical.lastDisconnect }

# Load-balancer logs may show that a socket/request existed earlier,
# but they are analytics/debug data, not the source of truth for presence.

rows: 历史断连时间+此刻在线

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户此刻是否在线、在哪台 Chat Server 持有连接的状态。它是实时状态，不适合只靠离线日志回答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Presence is the realtime state of whether a user is online and which Chat Server owns their connection. It should not be answered only from offline logs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 userId 存最近断连时间的持久化表。它回答“最后一次离线是什么时候”，不直接证明“现在在线”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The LastSeen table stores the latest disconnect time by userId. It answers when the user last went offline, not directly whether the user is online right now.

termDefinitions.meaning: LB 记录的连接或请求事件日志，适合审计、排障、流量分析；即使进入近实时分析系统，也不是聊天 presence 的权威读路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load-balancer logs are connection or request event logs used for audit, debugging, and traffic analysis. Even if streamed into a near-real-time analytics system, they are not the authoritative read path for chat presence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志在几秒到几分钟内进入分析系统并可查询；它比离线批处理快，但仍不是毫秒级产品状态查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Near-real-time analytics means logs become queryable within seconds to minutes. It is faster than offline batch, but still not a millisecond-level product-state query.

optionExplanations: 对：只有断开这一个事件才落一次库，查的时候另开一路去问对方现在还在不在，两路结果合并展示。
按分钟给全体在线用户做快照，写入量直接跟在线人数挂钩，跟「最小写入」的目标相反。
对方离线时 P2P 完全查不到结果，也没有服务端权限控制这层保护，不满足查询需求。
负载均衡器日志适合事后趋势分析，但答不出「此刻在不在线」这种实时问题。
optionExplanations_en: Right: write LastSeen only on disconnect, then on query read it in parallel with a Pub/Sub probe and merge — minimal writes while covering both history and live state.
Snapshotting every online user each minute ties write volume directly to online headcount, the opposite of minimizing writes.
Peer-to-peer questioning returns nothing when the other side is offline, and it also bypasses server-side permission control.
Load-balancer log analysis is fine for after-the-fact trends but can't answer "is this person online right now."

scenario: 用户从 Chat Server A 断开又连上 B，两台可能乱序地为他写断连时间戳。
scenario_en: A user drops off Chat Server A and reconnects to B, so the two hosts may write his disconnect timestamp out of order.
q: 两台服务器可能先后为同一用户写断连时间戳，如何防止旧值覆盖更新的值？
q_en: Two servers might write a disconnect timestamp for the same user out of order — how do you stop a stale value from overwriting a newer one?
options: 写之前抢一把全局锁
随机退避后再写
只允许固定一台服务器负责写这个字段，其余全部转发
DynamoDB 条件写：新时间戳更大才更新
options_en: Grab a global lock before writing
Write after a random backoff delay
Only ever let one fixed server write this field and forward everything else to it
A DynamoDB conditional write that only updates when the new timestamp is greater
why: 条件写把「比较再更新」压进存储层原子完成：晚到的旧时间戳会条件失败，不会倒退覆盖更近的断连时间。
why_en: A DynamoDB conditional write that only updates when the new timestamp is greater prevents two servers from racing and clobbering a more recent disconnect time.
codeSample:
UpdateItem LastSeen
  Key: { userId: "u_42" }
  SET lastDisconnect = :new
  ConditionExpression: :new > lastDisconnect
# fails harmlessly if another server already wrote a newer timestamp

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有满足指定条件（如新值大于旧值）才提交的写操作，由存储层原子完成「比较并更新」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write only commits when a stated condition holds, letting the store atomically compare and update in one step.

optionExplanations: 全局锁会把所有断连写入串行化，代价太大，也不是这里给出的方案。
随机退避降低碰撞概率，但不能保证旧值绝不覆盖新值，只是概率性缓解。
固定一台服务器负责写不现实——用户可能连在任意一台 Chat Server 上断开。
对：DynamoDB 条件写让「只有新时间戳更大才更新」在存储层原子完成，晚到的旧值会条件失败。
optionExplanations_en: A global lock would serialize every disconnect write — too costly, and not the mechanism actually used here.
Random backoff lowers the chance of a collision but doesn't guarantee an old value can never overwrite a newer one — only a probabilistic mitigation.
Pinning writes to one fixed server isn't realistic — a user can disconnect from whichever Chat Server they happened to be on.
Right: a DynamoDB conditional write makes "update only if the new timestamp is larger" atomic at the storage layer, so a late, stale write simply fails the condition.

scenario: 查看好友 last seen 时，库里的值可能已过时，而对方此刻可能正连着某台 Chat Server。
scenario_en: When you check a friend's last seen, the stored value may already be stale even though they might be connected to a Chat Server right now.
q: 客户端查询他人 last seen 的完整流程是？
q_en: What is the full flow when a client queries someone else's last seen?
options: 直接读 LastSeen 表并原样返回，不会去问对方当前是否真的在线
服务器并行读 LastSeen 表，同时经 Pub/Sub 探活，合并结果显示
向全部 Chat Server 广播查询再投票，开销随集群规模线性增长
轮询目标用户直到回应，请求持续阻塞等待，没有并行的历史兜底路径
options_en: Read the LastSeen table directly and return it as-is, without asking whether they are actually online right now
The server reads the LastSeen table and probes via Pub/Sub in parallel, then merges the results
Broadcast the query to every Chat Server and vote, with cost scaling linearly with cluster size
Poll the target user until it responds; the request blocks the whole time with no parallel historical fallback
why: 一次查询、两路并行响应（数据库的历史值 + 实时的在线确认），由客户端合并——存储与实时各答各的强项。
why_en: The server checks the last-seen table and in parallel forwards the query to the target's channel, and the client merges the database answer with any live online reply.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 请求者客户端
    participant A as Chat Server A
    participant DB as LastSeen 表
    participant B as Chat Server B（目标所在）
    C->>A: getLastSeen(target)
    par 并行
        A->>DB: 读最后断连时间
        A-->>C: updateLastSeen($DATE)
    and
        A->>B: 经 Pub/Sub 转发 getLastSeen
        B-->>C: updateLastSeen(ONLINE)（若在线）
    end
    C->>C: 合并：ONLINE 则绿点，否则显示断连时间

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

optionExplanations: 直接读表返回历史值，不会去确认对方此刻是否真的在线，查询不完整。
对：服务器并行读 LastSeen 表和经 Pub/Sub 问对方是否在线，两路结果由服务器合并后返回。
向全部 Chat Server 广播投票的开销随集群规模线性增长，不是这里选用的路径。
轮询直到回应会让请求一直阻塞等待，没有并行的历史兜底路径，体验也差。
optionExplanations_en: Reading the table alone and returning the stored value never confirms whether the person is actually online right now — an incomplete query.
Right: the server reads the LastSeen table and probes via Pub/Sub in parallel, then merges the two results before responding.
Broadcasting a vote to every Chat Server scales cost with cluster size — not the path used here.
Polling until a response blocks the request with no parallel historical fallback, and it's a poor experience besides.

scenario: WhatsApp 要显示联系人是否在线或最后在线时间。为少写库，方案只在用户断连时写 LastSeen 表；查询时并行读表并经 Pub/Sub 问对方是否在线。
scenario_en: WhatsApp needs to show whether a contact is online or their last-seen time. To minimize writes, the design writes the LastSeen table only on disconnect, and a query reads that table while asking over Pub/Sub in parallel whether the target is online.
q: 这个 last-disconnect 方案还剩哪些风险和补强？（多选）
q_en: What risks and mitigations remain for this last-disconnect design? (select all)
options: 两路响应可能先后到达，客户端要能等待或平滑更新 UI
Chat Server 崩溃时可能来不及写断连时间
补强：连接建立时也写一次 LastSeen 表
必须每秒刷新所有用户的 last seen
options_en: The two responses may arrive apart, so the client must wait or update the UI smoothly.
A Chat Server crash may happen before it writes the disconnect time.
Mitigation: also write the LastSeen row when a connection is established.
Every user's last seen must be refreshed every second.
why: 这个方案用少量写入换取近似在线状态，所以剩余风险在合并两路响应和断连上报可靠性。连接时也写一次 LastSeen 是低成本加固；每秒全量刷新会把写入量打爆。
why_en: The design saves writes, but the client must merge two responses and the server may miss a disconnect, so writing on connect adds a cheap safety net.
tradeoff: 最小写入量 vs 在线状态鲁棒性

termDefinitions.meaning: 只记录用户最近一次断开连接的时间，用它近似表示最后在线时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-disconnect means storing only the most recent time a user disconnected, as an approximation of last seen.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 userId 存最近断连或连接时间的表，用来回答最后在线时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A LastSeen table stores each user's latest connection-related timestamp for last-seen queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护用户长连接、转发实时消息并上报连接事件的服务节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Chat Server holds user connections, forwards realtime messages, and reports connection events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

optionExplanations: 两路响应到达有先后，客户端要能等待或平滑更新 UI，否则会闪烁或短暂显示错误状态。
Chat Server 崩溃时可能来不及写断连时间戳，这条时间就会停留在更早的值上。
连接建立时也写一次 LastSeen，是用极小的额外写入换取断连上报失败时的兜底。
每秒全量刷新所有用户会把写入量打爆，跟这个方案「最小写入」的目标正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: The two responses can arrive at different times, so the client needs to wait or update smoothly, or the UI flickers or briefly shows the wrong state.
If Chat Server crashes, it may not get to write the disconnect timestamp in time, leaving that value stuck on an earlier one.
Also writing LastSeen on connect trades a tiny extra write for a safety net when the disconnect report itself fails to land.
Refreshing every user's status every second would explode write volume, the opposite of this design's minimal-write goal.

scenario: 面试官按候选人级别（中级 / 高级 / Staff+）调整对广度与深度的期望比例。
scenario_en: Interviewers adjust their breadth-versus-depth expectations by candidate level (mid-level, senior, staff-plus).
q: 补全各级别期望的广度 : 深度比例：
q_en: Fill in the expected breadth-to-depth ratio at each level:
text: 面试期望的广度 : 深度——中级约 {{80}}:20、高级约 60:{{40}}、Staff+ 约 40:{{60}}；级别越高，越要主动识别问题并引领 deep dive，而不是等面试官来驱动。
why: 中级重广度、把功能跑通即可；高级要讲透伸缩与鲁棒性、比较分区策略的利弊；Staff+ 要 2-3 层深入故障模式、瓶颈甚至区域化架构。
why_en: Expectations shift from eighty-twenty breadth versus depth at mid-level, to sixty-forty at senior, to forty-sixty at staff-plus where you proactively lead the deep dives.

scenario: 写非功能需求前，你先问面试官「用户主要发 1:1 还是泡在大群里」——这既不是功能也不是非功能需求。面试官答：几乎全是 1:1。
scenario_en: Before writing non-functional requirements you ask the interviewer whether users mostly do one-to-one chats or live in big groups — neither a functional nor a non-functional requirement. The answer: almost all one-to-one.
q: 这个使用形态的答案主要用来定后面哪个设计？
q_en: Which later design decision does this usage-pattern answer mainly drive?
options: WebSocket 用 L4 还是 L7 负载均衡
附件上传走预签名 URL 还是存数据库
Pub/Sub 按 user 还是按 chat 分区
消息表主键该用 chatId 还是 messageId
options_en: Whether the WebSocket sits behind an L4 or L7 load balancer
Whether attachments upload via a pre-signed URL or the database
Whether pub/sub channels are partitioned by user or by chat
Whether the message table's primary key should be chatId or messageId
why: 1:1 主导就按 user 分区（每人 1 频道 1 订阅最省）；若面试官改口说主要是大群，答案翻转成按 chat 分区（省发布次数）。所以这个问题要在设计前问清，它的答案直接定分区策略。
why_en: One-to-one-dominant traffic points to partition-by-user; if the interviewer instead said mostly big groups, the answer flips to partition-by-chat, so you clarify it before designing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息层，发布者往频道发消息，所有订阅该频道的服务器都会收到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is a publish-subscribe layer where a publisher sends to a channel and every server subscribed to that channel receives the message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可随时双向收发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages either way after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: L4 在传输层按 TCP/IP 转发、不看内容；L7 能按 HTTP 路径和头路由，功能多但更重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An L4 load balancer forwards at the TCP layer without inspecting content, while an L7 one routes on HTTP paths and headers but is heavier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器签发的带临时授权的存储访问链接，客户端可直接上传或下载而无需额外鉴权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A pre-signed URL is a storage link the server signs to grant temporary, direct upload or download access without extra auth.

optionExplanations: L4/L7 的选择由「是否需要 L7 路由能力」决定，本题不需要，所以选 L4——和 1:1/群的比例无关。
附件走哪条路由「媒体需求」驱动，和会话是 1:1 还是群没关系。
对：1:1 主导按 user 分区订阅最省，大群主导则按 chat 省发布，使用形态直接决定它。
主键由查询模式（按 chat 查参与者）决定，不随 1:1/群比例变化。
optionExplanations_en: L4-versus-L7 is decided by whether you need L7 routing (you don't here, so L4), unrelated to the one-to-one/group mix.
The attachment path is driven by the media requirement, not by whether chats are one-to-one or group.
Right: one-to-one favors partition-by-user (cheapest subscriptions), big groups favor partition-by-chat, so usage pattern decides it.
The primary key is driven by query patterns (look up participants by chat), not by the one-to-one/group ratio.

scenario: 多设备改造后 Inbox 按 client 存，每台设备一份未投递队列。用户卖掉了旧平板，那个 client 再也不会连回来 ack，而你没有做停用（deactivate）机制。
scenario_en: After the multi-device change the Inbox is per-client, one undelivered queue for each device. A user sells an old tablet, so that client never reconnects to ack, and you have no deactivate mechanism.
q: 不给消失的客户端做停用，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if you never deactivate a client that's gone for good?
options: 账号登录态立刻失效，名下所有设备被强制下线重连
这台设备的 Inbox 没人 ack，只增不减，等 TTL 清
Pub/Sub 为每台失联设备保留常驻频道，越堆越多把内存吃满
同账号别的在线设备因共享送达状态而漏收这条消息
options_en: The account's login session is invalidated and all devices are force-reconnected
That device's Inbox only grows — nobody acks the messages, so they wait for the TTL
Pub/Sub keeps a standing channel per dead device, so channel-count memory balloons
Other online devices on the account miss this message due to shared delivery state
why: 正常路径靠设备 ack 清空自己的 per-client Inbox；设备永久消失后无人再 ack，那份队列只增不减，得等 30 天 TTL 兜底，期间白占存储与写吞吐。所以要主动停用消失的 client，并封顶约 3 台/账号。
why_en: A device normally acks to clear its per-client Inbox; one that's gone for good never acks, so its queue just grows until the TTL cleans it — so you deactivate dead clients.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多设备下每台设备一份的未投递消息队列，设备 ack 后对应条目被删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: With multiple devices the Inbox is a per-device queue of undelivered messages; an entry is deleted once that device acks it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号，用来清除 Inbox 里对应条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the client's confirmation that it received a message, used to clear the matching Inbox entry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储条目的存活时间，到期后被自动清理，这里设为 30 天。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the lifespan of a stored item, after which it is auto-deleted; here it is set to thirty days.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息层，Chat Server 订阅某频道后即可收到发往该频道的消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is a publish-subscribe layer; once a Chat Server subscribes to a channel it receives messages published there.

optionExplanations: 停用与否不影响账号登录能力，新设备照样注册进 Clients 表，不会触发全体下线。
对：设备不再连回来就永远不 ack，它那份 Inbox 删不掉、只增不减，只能靠 TTL 兜底，所以要主动停用。
频道仍按 userId 建、与设备数无关（多设备改造里 Pub/Sub 那侧不变），死设备不新增频道。
漏收是「按 user 单一 Inbox」才有的 bug；这里已是 per-client，别的设备有自己那份，不受影响。
optionExplanations_en: Deactivating or not doesn't affect login; a new device still registers in the Clients table, no mass logout.
Right: a gone device never acks, so its Inbox entries can't be deleted and only pile up until the TTL — hence deactivation.
Channels stay keyed by userId regardless of device count (the pub/sub side is unchanged), so dead devices add no channels.
Missing a message is the single-per-user-Inbox bug; here it's per-client, so other devices have their own copy and are fine.
